profiles.label: Jeep Gladiator / J-Series Pickup (SJ, 1963–1971 Gladiator-badged)
profiles.framing: This is a 1960s Kaiser-era work truck to be used as a weekend hauler and character driver around Carmel. Expect short runs to the beach, Carmel Valley errands, and occasional Highway 1 or Highway 68 grades. It is slow, loud, and heavy-steering, and most examples have single-circuit four-wheel drum brakes, so how well it stops and steers matters more than trim correctness. For a driver-grade buyer, the deciding factors are frame and cab rust, the health of whichever engine it has, the condition of the closed-knuckle front axle and steering, and a clean VIN and title trail for California registration. The particular Kaiser and AMC engines matter because their parts are scarcer than Chevy or Ford parts.
profiles.weak_points: ['Frame and cab-mount rust: Look at the rear frame crossmember, the rear spring hangers and shackle mounts, the cab mount areas, and the frame rails above the rear axle where mud packs. Coastal storage accelerates it. Patch plates, fresh undercoating, or POR-15 over scale can hide rot. Frame section and hanger repair runs $1,500–5,000. A rotted frame on a driver-value truck can be a walk-away issue. Ask for photos from directly under the truck and take a hammer or pick test at the PPI.', 'Cab and body rust: The usual spots are cab corners, rocker panels, door bottoms, floor pans (especially under the bench and pedals), the lower rear of the front fenders, windshield-frame and cowl leaks into the footwells, and Townside bed sides and wheel arches. Fiberglass or epoxy bed-side repairs and wavy bed floors are common. Reproduction panels are limited compared with Ford or Chevy trucks. Correct metal repair runs $3,000–15,000+ depending on extent. Ask for receipts showing metal replacement versus filler or fiberglass.', 'Tornado 230 OHC inline-six (1963–65): This Kaiser-specific overhead-cam engine is prone to oil leaks (valve cover, rear main), overheating, oil burning, and cam and rocker wear when oil changes were neglected. Internal parts are scarce, and many were swapped out decades ago. A rebuild runs $7,000–12,000+, partly because of parts hunting. Ask for compression and leak-down numbers and any rebuild receipts naming a machine shop.', "AMC 327 Vigilante V8 (1965–67, '65½ trucks): The common faults are worn rings and valve guides on high-mileage or unknown-mileage engines, causing blow-by, oil consumption, and plug fouling. The rocker-shaft valvetrain is noisy if oiling is poor. Rebuild parts exist but cost more and take longer to find than small-block Chevy parts. A rebuild runs $6,000–10,000. Get a cold-start video, compression and leak-down results, and an oil-consumption estimate from the seller.", 'Buick 350 Dauntless V8 (1968–71): This is a robust engine. Its known weak spot is the oil pump built into the timing cover, where wear can cause loss of prime and low hot oil pressure. Timing-chain stretch and coolant leaks at the timing cover are also common. Timing cover and pump service runs $800–1,800. Check hot-idle oil pressure with a mechanical gauge.', 'Closed-knuckle front axle (Dana 27/44 depending on model and year): Worn kingpin bearings or bushings and leaking knuckle-ball seals cause grease and gear-oil weep, wandering, and death wobble. Axle-shaft U-joints wear, and the knuckle balls get pitted. Manual locking hubs wear or seize. A full knuckle and kingpin rebuild runs $1,500–3,000. Ask for photos of the knuckle balls and any receipt for a kingpin or seal rebuild.', 'Steering: Manual (or optional power) steering boxes develop excessive play. Drag link and tie-rod ends wear, and steering-column bushings get sloppy. Lifted or added-leaf trucks often have altered steering geometry. Box rebuild or replacement runs $500–1,500, and linkage runs $300–800. Measure free play at the wheel during the PPI.', 'Brakes: Most trucks have four-wheel drums with no power assist. Through about 1966 they also have a single-circuit master cylinder, so one failed line means no brakes. Typical problems are corroded hard lines, seeping wheel cylinders, and stretched parking-brake cables. On Carmel Valley and Highway 1 grades this is the primary safety risk. A dual-circuit master conversion runs $500–1,500, and full hydraulic renewal runs $800–2,000. Ask for brake receipts with dates.', 'Transmission and transfer case: The column-shift three-speed (Warner T-90 type) or floor four-speed (T-98) can pop out of gear, especially second. Column linkage bushings wear. The Dana 20 transfer case leaks at the trans/case adapter and output seals, and its shift linkage can bind. Seals run $300–900. A transmission or transfer-case rebuild runs $1,500–3,500. An optional automatic (TH400 on V8 trucks) is durable but leaks.', 'Axles and driveline: Exp
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Change all fluids: engine oil and filter, transmission, Dana 20 transfer case, both differentials, and greasing of the front knuckles and kingpins', 'Brake inspection and full bleed, including wheel cylinders, hoses, hard-line corrosion, and shoe contamination from axle seals; adjust or replace the parking-brake cable', 'Replace tires if the date codes are over 6 years old, and balance the wheels; check wheel-bearing preload and repack the front and rear wheel bearings', 'Cooling system service: flush, thermostat, hoses, radiator cap, and fan belt; verify temperatures on a grade', 'Ignition tune-up check (points or dwell, timing, plugs) and carburetor adjustment; verify the electric fuel pump has fused, safe wiring and a shutoff', 'Replace or inspect all rubber fuel lines for ethanol deg

profiles.market_notes:
Factors that raise price:
- **Engine and drivetrain:** a V8 (AMC 327 '65½–67, Buick 350 '68–71) and four-wheel drive bring clear premiums over the Tornado OHC six or a two-wheel-drive truck.
- **Bed style:** Townside beds sell better than Thriftside (stepside).
- **Wheelbase:** the short-wheelbase J-2000/J-2500 is generally preferred over long beds and heavy-duty J-3000+ trucks as a driver.

Rough drivers with rust and oil consumption trade around $5,000–15,000. Honest, sorted drivers bring $20,000–35,000. Correct restorations and well-documented original-paint trucks reach $40,000–60,000+. Professionally built restomods can sell higher, but this buyer should value originality and receipts instead. Mileage is usually unknown and odometer-exempt, so condition, rust, and documentation drive price far more than miles. Rare details (early 327 trucks, factory colors like Nordic Blue, original data plates and literature) add collector interest but little driver value.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most surviving Gladiators have decades of deferred work: tired rubber everywhere, leaking seals throughout the driveline, single-circuit drum brakes, and brittle wiring. Even well-serviced trucks often need $3,000–7,000 of catch-up to be a dependable Carmel-area driver. Engines with unknown mileage and blow-by should be budgeted as future rebuild candidates.

Photos of the data plate, frame serial stamping, and both sides of the title showing matching numbers
Photos of the front knuckle balls and seals, or receipts for a kingpin/knuckle rebuild

profiles.label: Jeep Wrangler JK / JK Unlimited (2007–2018, incl. Rubicon & Rubicon X)
profiles.framing: For this buyer the JK Unlimited Rubicon is a dual-purpose tool: a Monterey-Peninsula daily that can run Los Padres fire roads, haul bikes and dogs, and go to the desert without drama. The Rubicon hardware (Rock-Trac 4:1, Tru-Lok front and rear lockers, electric sway-bar disconnect, Dana 44 front) is the reason to buy this trim rather than a Sport, and a 2014 gets the sorted 3.6 Pentastar plus the NSG370 six-speed. Because Wranglers are the most-modified vehicle in America, the real job is separating a documented, thoughtfully built truck from a bar-crawled parts-catalog project — and, in California, confirming the thing can actually be registered and smogged. Value here lives in records, geometry that doesn't shake, and a frame/underbody that hasn't been eaten by salt.
profiles.weak_points: 1) 3.6 Pentastar left-bank cylinder head (2011–early 2013 builds, worst before the revised casting): valve-seat/guide failure shows as cold ticking, misfire on cylinder 2 or 4, P0300/P0302/P0304 and a rough idle; head replacement is $2,500–$4,500. Chrysler extended coverage to 7yr/70k on many, so look for a dealer head-replacement invoice or confirm the engine build/casting date. A 2014 is largely past this, but any ticking deserves a compression/leak-down. 2) Oil filter housing / oil cooler assembly (plastic, Pentastar, ~60k+): cracks and warps, leaking oil down the rear of the block and coolant into the oil cooler; symptoms are oil smell, drips onto the exhaust, sometimes overheating. Aluminum aftermarket or updated Mopar unit, $500–$1,200 installed. If a seller claims it was done, get the invoice — this is the single most common Pentastar leak. 3) Death wobble: violent front-end oscillation after hitting a bump at 45–65 mph, caused by worn track bar bushings/bolt hole, loose track bar at the axle bracket, worn Dana 44 ball joints, or a poorly geometried lift. Ball joints are consumables at 60k–100k on lifted, big-tire trucks; $600–$1,400 per axle. Look for recent track bar, ball joint, and alignment receipts (the example listing shows lower ball joints at 92k — good sign, but ask what was left). 4) Steering box sector-shaft play and loose steering: vague on-center feel, clunk on turn-in; boxes wear at 80k–120k, often accelerated by 35s. Box $600–$1,200; a steering stabilizer is a band-aid, not a fix — a Falcon/adjustable stabilizer on a lifted JK can mask underlying wobble. 5) Frame and body rust: the JK frame rots at the rear lower control arm mounts, the skid plate/crossmember area, and around the rear body mounts and shock towers; door hinges, tailgate hinge, and windshield frame corners bubble. New-England/salt-belt cars (this example is NH-titled) need a lift-and-poke inspection with a screwdriver — perforation at a control arm mount is a structural repair, $2,000–$5,000 or a walk-away. 6) Water leaks: Freedom Top panel seals, hardtop-to-windshield and side-rail seals, door surrounds, and cowl drains all leak, soaking carpet and rusting the floor pan and seat brackets. Pull carpet edges and check for mud/moisture; sound-deadening foam installed under carpet (as here) can hide standing water. 7) NSG370 six-speed: notchy cold shifting is normal, but grinding into 3rd/4th, a heavy or dragging clutch, and a leaking or spongy hydraulic clutch slave (integral throwout bearing) are not. Clutch + slave is a transmission-out job, $1,500–$2,800. Fluid is a specific MTX spec and almost never changed. 8) Cooling and gaskets: plastic-tank radiators seep at 80k–120k ($400–$800), thermostat housing and water pump leak, and 3.6 valve cover/rear main seeps are common at high mileage. 9) TIPM / electrical gremlins (2011–2013 especially): fuel pump relay failure causing no-start or stalling, wipers or horn acting up; a bad TIPM is $600–$1,300. Also window regulators/motors, blend door actuators (clicking behind dash), and radio/Uconnect 730N nav units that fail or lose touch response ($400–$900 used/refurb). 10) Driveline vibration on lifted trucks: a 3.5" lift needs correct pinion angle, often front/rear driveshaft replacement (Adams shafts here are the right answer) and a slip-yoke/exhaust clearance check; leftover vibration usually means transfer case output seal wear, worn u-joints, or a bad rear main drive flange. 11) Exhaust manifold studs/bolts and heat shield rattle on Pentastars; broken studs cause a cold-start tick that mimics head failure. 12) Axles under big tires: front unit bearings (wheel hubs) go at 70k–120k with play/hum ($250–$450 each), Tru-Lok locker wiring and actuator connectors at the axle corrode and throw locker faults, and front axle inner C / knuckle wear shows up on rock-crawled trucks. 13) Gearing mismatch: stock 4.10s with 35s or larger without a regear makes the truck slow, hurts mpg, and increases clutch a
profiles.immediate_repairs: Tires (anything with 2015–2017 date codes is expired regardless of tread — five 35" DuraTracs mounted/balanced, $1,300–$1,900); full four-corner front-end inspection and re-torque/replace of track bar, ball joints, tie rod ends and drag link as needed ($400–$1,500); four-wheel alignment with caster set for the lift; oil filter housing/cooler inspection and replacement if the original plastic unit or if leaking ($500–$1,200); fluid catch-up — engine oil, NSG370 manual trans fluid, transfer case, front/rear Dana 44 diff fluid (Tru-Lok compatible), brake fluid flush, coolant ($500–$900); return intake/exhaust to CARB-legal or OEM configuration for CA smog plus registration paperwork ($600–$1,500); reseal Freedom Top and door surrounds, pull carpet to dry/inspect floors; battery and door/tailg
profiles.repairs_12mo: Radiator and/or thermostat housing seep, water pump; front unit bearings if any hum or play; steering box if on-center play persists or wobble recurs; clutch hydraulic slave/clutch if pedal is heavy or engagement is high at 95k+; rear main / valve cover seep monitoring; shock and control-arm bushing replacement on the lift kit (MetalCloak joints are serviceable but wear); brake pads/rotors on the aftermarket big-brake kit — verify pad availability and cost before buying; sway bar disconnect motor/actuator; blend door actuator and window regulator; underbody rust arrest and cavity wax on any salt-belt truck; possible regear to 4.88 if running 35s and the truck feels overgeared ($1,800–$2,800).
profiles.market_notes: Rubicon and Rubicon X command a clear premium over Sahara/Sport, four-door Unlimited over two-door, and 2012+ Pentastar over the 3.8; the manual adds want-it factor with enthusiasts but narrows the buyer pool, and high-mileage manuals carry clutch risk that buyers discount. Documented, tastefully modified trucks with receipts and correct driveline/geometry work sell near clean-stock money; parts-catalog builds with no paperwork, mismatched lift components, or an unresolved wobble history sell well below. Desirable colors (Anvil, Gobi, Firecracker Red, Hydro Blue) and a Freedom Top plus soft top help; salt-belt provenance, rust on frame or control arm mounts, and non-CARB emissions hardware are hard price penalties in California. Mileage bands matter less than in normal cars — condition, rust, and records dominate — but sub-80k Rubicons still bring a premium, and anything over 120k is priced as a driver/build platform.
profiles.catchup_notes: A 90k-mile JK Rubicon typically needs a full deferred-fluid pass (manual trans, transfer case, both diffs, brake fluid, coolant), a fresh set of correctly sized tires, and a complete front-end refresh — lifted big-tire trucks eat ball joints, track bars and unit bearings on a 60k–100k cycle. Budget for the Pentastar oil filter housing and a radiator if not already documented, plus reseal work on the top and door surrounds. On any salt-belt example, add underbody rust arrest and cavity wax as a first-year project regardless of how it looks from ten feet.

profiles.label: Jeep Wrangler JL / Wrangler Unlimited JL (incl. Willys, 2018-present)
profiles.framing: For a Carmel buyer, a JL Willys is a fun, top-off coastal and Big Sur cruiser with real trail ability for Hollister Hills or occasional Sierra trips. It is a utility toy, not a commuter appliance. On-road manners depend almost entirely on how intact and well-maintained the front suspension and steering are. The 3.6 V6 with the 6-speed manual is the purist combination, but every 2018-2023 manual is subject to a clutch recall that must be verifiably closed. Because this buyer prefers unmodified cars, a lifted or 'off-road modified' JL needs install records and a careful front-end inspection, or it should be priced as a project.
profiles.weak_points:
1) Front-end 'death wobble' and wandering: the JL solid front axle is sensitive to a worn or under-damped steering damper, a loose or worn front track bar and its bushings, tie-rod and drag-link ends, ball joints, and incorrect caster after a lift. FCA issued revised steering dampers and several service bulletins for 2018-2021 trucks. Symptoms are violent shake after a bump at 45-60 mph, or a vague on-center feel. Fixes range from $300 (damper) to $800-1,500 (track bar, tie rod, drag link) to $2,000+ if a lift has to be corrected. Look for alignment sheets and records of the damper update.

2) Manual clutch pressure-plate recall: 2018-2023 JL and Gladiator 6-speed manuals were recalled because the pressure plate can overheat and fracture. The first remedy was a software update that adds a 'clutch hot' warning. A follow-up hardware remedy replaced the clutch and pressure plate. Require dealer proof that both are complete. Outside the recall, a clutch job runs $1,800-2,800. Also watch for clutch hydraulics (master/slave) issues: a soft or sinking pedal.

3) Pentastar 3.6 oil filter housing and oil cooler: the plastic assembly cracks or its gasket seeps oil and coolant into the valley. This is common from 40-80k miles and costs $500-900. Smell for hot oil and look down the back of the intake.

4) Pentastar water pump and thermostat housing seep. The water pump is timing-chain driven on the 3.6, so it is about $700-1,200. Check for pink crust at the front of the engine.

5) Steering gear box: leaks and free play develop, especially with larger tires. A box costs $900-1,600 installed. On 2018 trucks, also confirm the frame steering-gear-bracket weld recall.

6) Front axle wear: unit bearings ($350-600 per side), ball joints ($600-1,000), and axle-tube seals. Larger tires accelerate all of it. The rear Trac-Lok limited-slip needs the correct friction-modified fluid. Check for chatter in tight turns.

7) Lifts, larger tires, and wheel offset: these drive steering wear and incorrect speedometer readings. Tires of 35 inches or more on stock gears make the manual sluggish and hard on the clutch. A regear costs $2,500-3,500. Ask what parts were used and who installed them.

8) Water intrusion: Freedom Top panel seals, door seals, cowl, and windshield-frame seals leak, and the carpet holds water. Look for musty odor, damp foam, corrosion on under-seat connectors, and rust on floor pan bolts. Seals and adjustment cost $200-800.

9) Windshield cracks: common, and the JL windshield is expensive. Replacement is $600-1,500, more if a camera calibration is needed on optioned trucks.

10) Aluminum doors, hood, fenders, and tailgate: look for galvanic corrosion or bubbling where they meet steel hinges and fasteners. Also check for off-road dents to rock rails and skid plates.

11) Underbody trail damage: dented skid plates, a bent tie rod or drag link, scraped differential covers, a crushed muffler, and a dented gas tank skid. A Willys was marketed for trail use, so assume it was used that way.

12) Electrical and infotainment: Uconnect freezes or reboots, the backup camera drops out, and TPMS faults appear after wheel swaps. Automatic trucks with Engine Stop-Start add a small auxiliary battery that fails every 3-4 years ($150-300) and throws ESS or electrical warnings.

13) Transfer case and driveshafts: on the Command-Trac part-time case, check for a stiff or grinding 4H/4L shift and fluid leaks. Front driveshaft CV/U-joint wear accelerates on lifted trucks.

14) Coastal and salt exposure: Carmel fog plus any snow-country history matters. Inspect frame rails, crossmembers, brake lines, and exhaust hangers for scale. Check the title and Carfax history for Midwest or Northeast registration.
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Verify and complete any open recalls, especially the manual clutch pressure-plate software and hardware remedies.', 'Torque-check front track bar, steering damper, tie rod/drag link and control arm bolts, especially if lifted.', 'Four-wheel alignment with caster check; replace steering damper if weak or original pre-update part.', 'Change front and rear differential fluid (friction modifier in rear Trac-Lok), transfer case fluid, and manual transmission fluid.', 'Engine oil and filter, engine air filter, cabin filter; inspect oil filter housing for seepage.', 'Brake fluid flush and brake inspection (larger tires wear pads faster).', 'Inspect and rotate or replace mud-terrain tires (cupping, chunking, age); balance to cure vibration.', 'Reseal and adjust Freedom Top panels and door seals;
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Oil filter housing/cooler assembly replacement if seeping ($500-900).', 'Front end parts: tie rod ends, track bar bushings, ball joints as play develops ($400-1,500).', 'Front wheel hub/unit bearings if humming or showing play ($350-600 per side).', 'Tire replacement, often due on modified Jeeps with worn mud-terrains ($1,000-1,800 per set).', 'Main or auxiliary battery replacement ($150-350).', 'Coolant service and water pump if any weep appears ($700-1,200 if pump needed).', 'Windshield replacement if chipped or cracked ($600-1,500).', 'Undo or correct poorly done modifications (lift correction, steering correction, return to stock) ($500-3,000).']
profiles.market_notes: Price moves on body style (4-door Unlimited is the norm), trim (Rubicon > Sahara > Willys > Sport), and top (hardtop and Sky One-Touch command premiums over soft top). Mileage bands are under 30k, 30-60k, and over 60k. The 6-speed manual is rarer but trades flat to slightly below automatics in the broad market, so enthusiasts can buy it well. Modifications rarely add value and often subtract it for documented-stock buyers. A clean, stock, one-owner truck with dealer records and closed recalls is worth a meaningful premium. The ~$23k result on the example reflects high miles, mods, or condition questions more than strong demand.
profiles.catchup_notes: A 2022 is young but often trail-used. Expect a full driveline fluid service (diffs, transfer case, gearbox), an alignment, and a front-end bolt torque and inspection. Confirm the clutch recall is complete. On a modified truck, budget to correct or return to stock any poorly matched lift, steering, or tire setup before trusting it on Highway 1.

profiles.label: Lamborghini Diablo (pre-facelift 1990–1998: base 2WD, VT, SE30, SV, VT Roadster)
profiles.framing: A pre-facelift Diablo is a hand-built carbureted-era-thinking V12 exotic with fuel injection bolted on. As a 'driver' it rewards someone who accepts a heavy clutch, poor rear visibility, marginal A/C, and specialist-only maintenance, and who drives it often enough to keep seals and fuel components alive. For a Carmel, CA buyer the two make-or-break issues come before mechanics. The first is proven California registrability: US/CARB-certified spec versus gray-market, since California has no rolling smog exemption for post-1975 cars. The second is a documented recent clutch, fuel-system, and cooling refresh by a known Lamborghini specialist. Originality matters even for a driver, because modified or Euro/Gulf-converted cars are both harder to register and harder to resell.
profiles.weak_points: ["Clutch and flywheel. The single-plate (twin-plate on some) clutch is heavy and wears quickly with traffic, hill starts, and valet abuse, often lasting 8k–15k miles depending on driver. Replacement on the Diablo's forward-mounted gearbox layout is a major labor job, commonly $10k–$20k at a specialist with flywheel resurface, release bearing, and hydraulics. Get a dated receipt with mileage and ask for a measured engagement point or remaining-life estimate from the last shop.", 'Clutch hydraulics. Master and slave cylinders and the long hydraulic line weep, causing a sinking pedal, high engagement, or difficulty selecting gears hot. It is a cheap part but labor-intensive ($1.5k–$4k), and it is often done together with the clutch. Look for fluid stains in the cabin footwell and at the bellhousing.', 'Fuel system and fire risk. Aged rubber fuel hoses, injector O-rings, fuel rail seals, regulators, and twin pumps leak onto a hot V12 and exhaust, and engine-bay fires are a known Diablo failure mode. Hoses older than about 10 years should be presumed due. A full fuel-system reseal with pumps, filters, regulators, and injector service runs $5k–$12k. Demand an itemized receipt and photos of new lines, and smell for raw fuel after a hot shutdown.', 'Cooling system. Twin side-mounted aluminum radiators in the rear haunches corrode and clog. Fan motors, fan relays, and thermo switches fail, the water pump weeps, and long coolant pipes and hoses age, all of which leads to overheating in traffic and on long idles. Radiator pair plus hoses runs roughly $4k–$9k, and a water pump job $2k–$5k. Verify fan operation and stable temps after 20+ minutes of idle.', 'Timing chains, tensioners, and valve clearances. The Bizzarrini-derived 5.7 V12 uses chains. Stretched chains or tired tensioners rattle on cold start, and neglected valve clearances (checked roughly every 15k miles or by age) cause poor running. A chain/tensioner job is $8k–$20k. A full engine rebuild after chain or valve failure is $60k–$120k+. Ask for valve-adjustment records and compression/leakdown numbers.', 'Engine oil leaks and top-end gaskets. Cam cover, intake plenum, throttle body, and rear main/sump gaskets seep with age, and oil on exhaust adds fire risk. Throttle-body and plenum gaskets on early LIE-injected cars are common. Budget $2k–$8k depending on what is apart.', 'Ignition and engine management (early cars). 1990–1993 cars use distributors, caps, rotors, and plug wires, along with crank, timing, and coolant-temperature sensors on the Lamborghini LIE management. Sensor failures cause no-starts, stalling, or rough idle. Parts are individually modest ($500–$3k), but diagnosis needs a specialist who knows LIE, since there is no generic OBD scan on most of these cars.', 'Gearbox. The gated 5-speed is notoriously stiff when cold. Worn 2nd/3rd synchros grind, and shift linkage bushings wear, adding slop. A gearbox rebuild runs $10k–$25k. Stiff when cold is normal; grinding when hot or jumping out of gear is not.', 'VT-specific: viscous coupling, front differential, and front halfshafts (VT, VT Roadster, later SV-adjacent cars). Viscous couplings degrade, causing binding on tight turns or no torque transfer. Front diff seals leak and CV boots tear. Coupling or front-diff work runs $5k–$15k+. A 2WD base car avoids this entirely.', 'Chassis and crash repair. The tubular steel spaceframe carries aluminum doors/hood and composite panels. Frame tubes rust at low points and around the radiator areas, and many Diablos have hidden crash or nose damage from low ground clearance. Frame straightening or tube replacement is open-ended ($10k–$50k+). Look for panel-gap irregularity, overspray, kinked or welded tubes, and repainted engine-bay frame.', 'Suspension, steering, and brakes. Rubber bushings, ball joints, and shocks are worn on most cars at this age, and steering rack ends wear too. Early cars lack ABS, and large calipers stick when cars sit. Steel brake lines and soft lines age
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Full fluid service: engine oil and filter, gearbox oil, coolant flush (if undocumented within 2 years), brake and clutch fluid flush; plus VT front diff and viscous coupling fluid check on VT cars', 'Fuel-system inspection and replacement of any original or aged rubber fuel hoses, clamps, and injector seals if no receipt within ~5–10 years; add a fuel smell check and an onboard fire extinguisher', 'Tire date-code check and replacement if older than ~6 years, regardless of tread', 'Battery, battery cutoff/tender setup, and cleaning or tightening of main grounds and the fuse/relay board', "Door gas strut replacement if doors sag or won't stay up", 'Cooling fan and relay verification, thermostat check, and correction of any coolant seeps', 'Brake inspection, including freeing sticking calip
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Clutch, flywheel resurface, and release bearing if the remaining-life estimate is under ~30–40% or the receipt is older than ~8–10 years', 'Clutch master and slave cylinder replacement if original or undocumented', 'Valve clearance check and adjustment if no record within ~15k miles or 5+ years', 'Suspension bushing, ball joint, and shock refresh if original', 'Radiator pair and coolant hose replacement if original or corroded', 'A/C service or conversion, compressor and seals', 'Window regulators and motors, pop-up headlight motors, and gauge repairs', 'Cam cover, plenum, and sump gasket reseal if seeping', 'CV boots and halfshaft service, plus front diff seals on VT cars', 'Exhaust manifold and heat shield inspection and repair']
profiles.market_notes: Price is driven first by spec and originality. SE30 and Jota command large premiums, SV and VT Roadster sit above base and VT coupes, and early base 2WD cars are prized by purists. US-spec, CARB-legal cars with original paint in period colors (Rosso, Giallo, Nero, Viola on SE30) and factory wheels outrank gray-market or Gulf-converted, repainted, or 'updated' cars. 6.0 headlight swaps, aftermarket wings, aftermarket exhausts, and non-original upholstery noticeably cut value and buyer pool. Documented clutch, fuel-system, and cooling work by a recognized Lamborghini specialist, plus continuous records, can swing value by tens of thousands. Very low mileage helps less than you'd expect unless it comes with evidence of regular exercise and recent age-related service.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most pre-facelift Diablos are 30+ years old with low annual mileage, so age rather than miles drives the work. Expect perished fuel and coolant hoses, sticky calipers, tired bushings, seeping gaskets, and weak electrics even on low-odometer cars. Plan $15k–$35k of catch-up on a car without recent itemized specialist records, more if the clutch or radiators are original.

profiles.label: Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica (LP640-2, 2023–2024)
profiles.framing: The Tecnica is the last road-focused, rear-drive Huracán. It uses the STO's 631-hp naturally aspirated V10, rear-wheel steering and LDVI chassis software in a street-usable body. For a Carmel driver it is a weekend and Highway 1 car, not a garage queen. The deciding factors are dealer-documented annual services, clean diagnostic readouts (especially DCT clutch wear), the condition of the carbon-ceramic brakes, and a verified, transferable factory or Selezione warranty. The 7-speed DCT is the only transmission offered, so an automatic is expected and is not a negative. Prefer an unmodified, non-tracked, front-lift-equipped car with a clean nose and underbody.
profiles.weak_points: ["7-speed LDF dual-clutch transmission (Graziano unit, related to the Audi R8 S tronic): clutch packs wear faster with launch control, track use, and frequent low-speed creeping in traffic or on driveways. Wear is tracked as a percentage that a Lamborghini dealer or Audi-level diagnostic tool can read. Clutch replacement means removing the transmission, roughly $10k–20k out of warranty. A mechatronic or full transmission failure runs about $25k–45k. Symptoms include shudder pulling away, harsh 1–2 or reverse engagement, 'gearbox fault' or limp mode, and slow reverse selection. Ask for a recent clutch-wear printout and records of any software updates.", 'Carbon-ceramic brakes (CCM, standard on the Tecnica): rotors wear by oxidation and mass loss, so thickness alone is not the full picture. Heavy track use, or repeated hard stops without cooldown, can produce surface cracking around the drill holes and edge chipping. A full rotor set is roughly $20k–30k; pads run about $2.5k–5k per axle with labor. Ask for a dealer rotor wear or weight measurement and close-up photos of all four rotor faces.', 'Front axle lift system (optional, and nearly essential for coastal and hillside driveways): failures show up as a slow or no-lift condition, hydraulic leaks at the front strut lift collars, or pump and valve faults that set warnings. Expect about $2.5k–8k depending on whether the pump, the struts or both are affected. Cycle the lift several times during the inspection and look for fluid at the strut tops.', "Nose, splitter and front radiators: the Tecnica's revised front fascia is low and costly. Curb, ramp and debris strikes crack the splitter, scuff the underbody aero and damage the radiators and condensers behind the intakes. A fascia with paint runs about $8k–15k+, and each radiator or condenser about $2k–4k installed. Check for fresh paint, mismatched PPF, bent fins and coolant traces.", 'Tecnica-specific carbon and body parts: the carbon engine cover (matte carbon on many cars), fixed rear wing, rear diffuser and side intakes are expensive. Matte carbon scratches and cannot be polished like gloss. A replacement engine cover alone can reach about $10k–20k. Look for chips, clearcoat hazing, and stress cracks around the mounting points.', "5.2L V10 (dual port and direct injection) is fundamentally robust but needs on-time annual service. Lamborghini's interval is 12 months or 15,000 km (about 9,300 mi), whichever comes first. Watch for ignition coil or plug misfires (coil pack about $300–500 each, a full set of plugs and coils about $3k–5k), seepage at the cam covers, oil sump and DCT housing, and occasional injector faults. Some oil consumption is normal, so check the level with the dash-based procedure. Ask for dealer invoices for every interval, including fluid specs.", 'Rear-wheel steering and LDVI electronics: rear-steer actuator faults, steering-angle calibration errors after alignment or curb strikes, and chassis warnings. These show up as a crooked wheel, a darty feel at speed or a stability-control warning. An alignment needs Lamborghini-specific calibration. A full module scan is essential.', 'Low-voltage sensitivity and battery drain: the Huracán has notable parasitic draw. Weeks without a tender can flatten the battery and trigger cascading electronic faults, including gearbox, lift and infotainment errors. A battery is about $500–1,200 depending on type. Confirm the car was kept on a CTEK-type maintainer and check the battery health.', 'Infotainment and HMI (8.4-inch center touchscreen with Alexa and CarPlay): freezing, reboots, CarPlay dropouts, and rear camera or nose-lift memory glitches are typically fixed with dealer software updates. Hardware replacement is about $3k–6k. Check that software campaigns are complete.', 'Center-lock forged wheels (common option): the hubs and center nuts require the correct torque tool and procedure. Incorrect torque from a tire shop can damage the hub threads or let a nut back off. Insp
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Annual service if it is due or near due by time or mileage (oil, filters, multi-point inspection), roughly $1,800–3,500 at a Lamborghini dealer', 'Brake fluid flush if more than 2 years old or the car has been driven hard (about $300–600)', 'Battery load test and installation of a quality maintainer (CTEK or similar), with a battery replacement if it is weak', 'Full-system diagnostic scan, including DCT clutch-wear values; complete any open recalls or software campaigns at the dealer', 'Four-wheel alignment with rear-steer calibration if tire wear is uneven or the steering wheel is off-center', 'Tires if worn or older than 4–5 years; Tecnica-specific Bridgestone Potenza Sport or OE-spec tires run about $2,000–3,000 per set mounted', 'PPF repair or new front-end film plus a paint touch-up
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Next annual or 15,000 km service, roughly $1,800–3,500, plus a larger interval service if due (spark plugs, air filters), roughly $3,500–7,000', 'Rear tires again for a regularly driven car; rears can last only 5k–10k miles (about $1,000–1,600 for a pair)', 'DCT oil and filter service per the Lamborghini schedule if the car is approaching the time interval (about $1,000–2,000)', 'Cabin and engine air filters and wiper blades if not done at the last service', 'Front lift strut seal or pump service if early seepage is noted (about $2.5k–8k)', 'Alcantara steering wheel cleaning or retrim, plus seat bolster care (about $200–2,000)', 'Possible ignition coil replacement if a misfire code appears (about $300–500 per coil)']
profiles.market_notes: Mileage is the biggest price driver. Sub-5k-mile cars carry a strong premium, while examples with 20k+ miles trade at a meaningful discount even with warranty. The arrival of the hybrid Temerario has firmed up demand for the last naturally aspirated V10 Huracáns, especially well-specced Tecnicas. Value rises with desirable options (front lift, matte or gloss carbon packages, center-lock forged wheels, Sensonum audio, Ad Personam or hero colors such as greens and oranges), a transferable warranty to 2026–2027 or beyond, full Lamborghini dealer service records, and clean Carfax and paint-meter results. Track history, front-end repaint, aftermarket exhaust or tunes, missing lift, and incomplete dealer records all reduce price noticeably.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most examples are only 1–3 years old, so catch-up is mainly about confirming annual dealer services were done on time by date, not just mileage. It also means flushing brake fluid at the 2-year mark and completing open recalls and software campaigns. High-mileage, frequently driven cars also need attention to tires, front-end chip protection and clutch-wear trends before the warranty expires.

profiles.label: Lancia Delta HF Integrale Evoluzione II (Evo 2)
profiles.framing: This is the final, catalyzed 215hp development of the homologation-bred Integrale, and at current money it is a blue-chip Group A icon that the buyer intends to actually drive on Carmel Valley Road and Highway 1 — not park in a bubble. For this buyer the car must be a documented, unmolested, rust-free, numbers-correct Evo 2 with a legible ownership chain from Europe through import, because originality and provenance carry most of the value and almost all of the resale risk. Mechanically it is a hand-built Fiat-group turbo four with a demanding service clock: it rewards a fastidious owner and punishes deferred maintenance brutally. The decision hinges far more on rust, authenticity paperwork, and service history than on odometer reading.
profiles.weak_points: ['Structural and cosmetic rust is the number one killer. Check the front strut towers and inner fender seams, the sills at the jacking points, the floor pans under the front carpets (water gets in past the plenum/scuttle drains and the windshield seal), the rear inner arches behind the boxed Evo fender flares, the tailgate lower edge and around the rear wiper motor, the sunroof drain channels if fitted, and the fuel filler bowl. Cars that lived in Northern Europe or spent winters in Italy are commonly patched. Proper metalwork plus a color-matched respray on a Blue Lagos car runs $8,000–30,000 and permanently dents value; look for old bodyshop invoices, paint-depth-gauge readings and photos of the car on a lift with the arch liners out.', 'Cambelt service is time-based, not mileage-based. The interval is roughly every 3 years or 36,000 km, and a snapped belt on this interference 16V head means bent valves and a $6,000–12,000 head rebuild. A 2020 belt on a 2026 car is out of date regardless of the 41,000 km on the clock. Demand a dated invoice covering belt, tensioner, water pump, and ideally the balance-shaft/auxiliary belt, from a shop that knows Lancias.', 'Head gasket failure and warped/cracked cylinder heads are classic Integrale problems, aggravated by overboost, poor coolant maintenance, and cars that sit. Symptoms: coolant loss with no external leak, pressurized expansion tank, mayonnaise under the cam cover, hot-idle misfire. Budget $4,000–8,000 for head off, skim, gasket, and valve work; a full bottom-end rebuild with pistons and rods is $18,000–30,000 at a specialist.', 'Turbo and boost control. The Garrett T3 (water-cooled) suffers shaft play and seal failure from hot shutdowns and stale oil; the wastegate actuator, boost solenoid and the vacuum/boost hose spaghetti perish and cause overboost cuts or soft running. Evo 2 cars also crack the cast exhaust manifold between runners. Turbo rebuild/replacement $2,000–4,500; manifold $1,200–2,500 with labor; hose renewal kit plus tuning $800–1,500.', 'Driveline: the Ferguson viscous center coupling degrades with age and low use, and a seized or dead VC gives tight-turn binding, driveline wind-up or vague traction; the Torsen rear diff can whine and its output seals leak. The five-speed transaxle is weak on second-gear synchro and suffers a notchy/obstructive shift from worn linkage bushings and a tired clutch hydraulic system. VC $2,000–3,500 installed, gearbox rebuild $4,500–8,000, clutch (dual-mass-free but labor-heavy) $1,800–3,000.', 'Cooling system and hot-running. Radiator, intercooler-to-throttle plumbing, the header/expansion tank and its cap, and the electric fan switch are all failure-prone; these cars run hot in traffic and a late fan is how heads get warped. Plan on a new radiator, hoses, thermostat, cap and fan relay as a matter of course — $1,500–2,500.', 'Bosch ABS system (ATE/Bosch hydraulic unit, accumulator and pump). A pulsing or permanently lit ABS light usually means a dead accumulator or pump motor; parts are scarce, and a rebuilt unit is $1,500–3,500. Test brake pedal feel and warning-light behavior cold and after a drive.', 'Electrics and grounds. Corroded earth points behind the battery tray and in the footwells cause phantom faults: dash warning lights, power window failure, erratic fuel gauge, fan and fuel-pump relay dropouts. The Marelli/Weber IAW ECU is generally robust but the crank sensor, air-temp sensor and injector harness insulation age out. Body ECU/relay board issues and the 5-digit odometer make mileage verification a documentation exercise, not an instrument-cluster one.', 'Interior trim is fragile and largely NLA. Dash tops crack, the Recaro bolsters and Crème leather on Blue Lagos cars stain and split, the center-dash oil pressure/temp gauge pod fades, headliners droop, and Evo-specific items (hood vents, adjustable rear spoiler, flare trim, Speedline Montecarlo center caps, correct Momo wheel) are expensive or unobtainable. Faded or
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Fresh timing belt, tensioner, water pump and auxiliary belts regardless of the last invoice date if it is over ~3 years old ($1,500–2,800)', 'Four new tires in correct 205/45ZR16 fitment plus alignment and corner-weight-sane setup ($1,400–2,200)', 'Full fluid service: engine oil, gearbox/transaxle, rear diff, coolant flush, brake and clutch fluid ($600–1,200)', 'Brake system refresh — flex lines, pads, bleed, and rotor inspection; ABS accumulator function test ($900–2,500)', 'Replace all vacuum/boost hoses and check boost solenoid and wastegate operation; road-tune to spec boost ($600–1,500)', 'Battery, grounds cleanup, and relay/fuse box inspection; fix any dash warning lights ($300–900)', 'Fuel filter, and on a low-use car an in-tank pump and hose inspection plus injector cleaning ($40

profiles.market_notes: Evo 2 sits at the top of the Integrale ladder, and within it the special editions — Blue Lagos, Giallo Ginestra, Bianco Perlato, Dealers Collection, Club HF Collection — carry a large premium over standard Rosso/Nero cars, with documented low-km, single-repaint-free examples now trading well into six figures. Provenance is price: a Lancia registry entry, original libretto/Fahrzeugbrief, matching engine and chassis numbers, an unbroken service file with dated cambelt invoices, and clean import paperwork can be worth 20–40% versus an undocumented car. Rust history, a respray, replaced Evo-specific trim, or a converted lesser Integrale destroy value disproportionately; conversely high-km but immaculate, heavily documented driver cars trade at a steep discount to museum-km cars and are often the better buy for someone who will actually use it. Manual is the only transmission; RHD conversions and non-original turbo/ECU tuning are discounts.
profiles.catchup_notes: Even a 26k-mile Evo 2 is a 30-plus-year-old Italian turbo car whose rubber, fluids and fuel system have aged on the calendar rather than the odometer, so assume a full recommissioning: cambelt package, all coolant/vacuum/fuel hoses, tires, brake and clutch hydraulics, fluids, and battery/grounds. Low-mileage cars that sat are often worse than driven ones for seals, tank varnish, seized calipers and flat-spotted bushings. Budget roughly $6,000–10,000 of catch-up in the first year on a well-kept example, more if the A/C, ABS accumulator or viscous coupling need attention.

profiles.label: Land Rover Defender 110 (L663, 2020+)
profiles.framing: The L663 Defender 110 is an aluminum-monocoque luxury SUV with genuine off-road hardware. For a Carmel buyer it is a comfortable daily driver and weekend tool for Big Sur, the coast and trailheads. It is not a simple, owner-serviceable truck. Early 2020-2021 cars carry the most software, electrical and recall baggage, and most are now past the 4yr/50k factory warranty. Documented dealer software updates, recall completion, remaining CPO coverage, and a clean full-system scan matter more than cosmetics or mileage alone.
profiles.weak_points: ['Early-build electrical and software instability (2020-2021 especially). Symptoms include Pivi Pro screen freezes or reboots, a blank instrument cluster, intermittent key-fob and keyless-entry faults, and camera or parking-aid dropouts. Many cases were fixed by dealer or OTA software reflashes, but some needed module replacement. A head unit or cluster costs roughly $2,000-4,500 out of warranty. Look for dealer repair orders showing software updates and module replacements.', "12V and auxiliary battery drain. Early cars were notorious for flat batteries after sitting, which trigger cascading false warnings. Often cured by software plus new batteries. Main 12V battery $350-600, auxiliary battery $250-450 installed. Repeated battery replacements in the records point to an unresolved parasitic draw or module that won't sleep.", '48V mild-hybrid system (P400 inline-6 and later P300 MHEV). The belt-integrated starter-generator, 48V battery and DC-DC converter can fault. Symptoms are stop/start inoperative, charging warnings or no-start. Repair runs roughly $1,500-4,500 depending on component. A scan for 48V/BISG codes is essential.', 'Ingenium engine coolant leaks. The 3.0 inline-6 (P400) and 2.0 four-cylinder (P300) are known for seeping plastic coolant pipes, turbo coolant feed/return lines (superseded revised parts exist), and thermostat housing and auxiliary pump leaks. Symptoms are a sweet smell, a low-coolant message, and crusted residue around the turbo and rear of the head. Pipe repairs cost $400-1,800. Ignored leaks risk overheating and head or engine damage. Ask for the part number of any updated lines installed.', 'Ingenium engine and timing-chain risk. The chain is mounted at the rear of the engine, so chain or guide service is engine-out labor. Any engine replacement is roughly $18,000-30,000. The risk is low-frequency but real, and it rises with extended oil-change intervals, low oil level or poor-quality oil. Look for 7,500-10,000 mile or annual oil changes with correct-spec oil, not just the maximum-interval dealer schedule.', "Air suspension (standard on most US 110s). Air springs can leak (overnight sagging, uneven height), compressors wear out from overwork, and valve blocks and height sensors fail, bringing up a 'Suspension fault' or 'Reduced ride height' message. Costs are roughly $900-1,600 per air spring and $1,500-2,800 for a compressor at a dealer, less at an independent. Check that all height modes, access height and off-road height reach target and hold overnight.", 'Two-speed transfer case and differentials. Land Rover has issued transfer-case service and updates. Fluid neglect, or tire mismatch across axles, stresses the transfer case and center coupling. The optional active rear e-locker has actuator faults. A transfer case replacement is $4,000-7,000. Look for receipts for transfer-case, front and rear differential fluid changes, and any software update to the transfer case.', "ZF 8HP 8-speed automatic. The unit itself is robust, but it is marketed as 'lifetime fill.' A fluid and pan/filter service around 60-80k is prudent and costs $600-1,000. Harsh 2-3 shifts, flare or delayed engagement on a high-mileage car with no service record warrant caution.", 'Water ingress. Leaks show up at the side-hinged rear door seal, the sliding panoramic roof drains, the folding fabric roof (if fitted), and the Alpine roof lights. Symptoms are damp carpets, musty smells, fogged lamps and random electrical faults from wet connectors under the carpets or in the rear quarter. Fixes range from $200 for drain clearing to thousands if a module or harness is corroded.', "Rear door and exterior-mounted spare. The heavy side-hinged door carries the full-size spare, so check for door sag, a worn check strap, and misaligned latch or seal. Oversized aftermarket spares accelerate wear. Also inspect the aluminum body for galvanic corrosion where steel fasteners, the tow hitch or accessories contact aluminum. This matters more in C

profiles.market_notes: P400 inline-6 cars (SE, HSE, X, First Edition) bring more than P300 four-cylinder base and S cars. V8 and 130 models sit in a different price tier. Remaining transferable LR CPO coverage (7yr/100k from original in-service date) adds real money on 2020-2021 cars. So do documented recall and software completion and a clean Carfax, while prior LR 'buyback' or heavy repair history sharply discounts. Desirable options and packs include Off-Road Pack with e-locker, Towing Pack, Explorer or Adventure packs, the 3rd-row seat, and colors like Pangea Green, Gondwana Stone and Tasman Blue. Plain white or black cars with high miles (80k+) trade at a notable discount, and aftermarket lifts or tunes usually hurt resale to mainstream buyers.
profiles.catchup_notes: A typical 2020-2021 example at 60-90k is past factory warranty and often has only dealer 'lifetime fluid' maintenance. Expect to catch up on the transfer case, differentials, transmission fluid, coolant, spark plugs and brake fluid ($1,500-3,000 total). Also verify all software and recall updates, and replace aging 12V/aux batteries. Budget for at least one coolant-leak fix and one air-suspension or electrical module repair within the first couple of years.

profiles.label: Land Rover Defender 110 / Land Rover 110 (Otokar, Turkey, c.1987–2000)
profiles.framing: This is a slow, loud, crude, and very capable coil-sprung 4x4. It makes sense for this buyer as a weekend and utility driver around Carmel, Big Sur, and Carmel Valley, not as a freeway commuter. Realistic cruising is 60–65 mph, and the salt-air coastal environment will keep working on any rust that is already present. Otokar trucks are license-built in Turkey, and most US examples are recent 25-year imports that were cosmetically refreshed and often re-engined, so 'unmodified' is rare. A well-documented, properly executed Tdi conversion is usually a net positive for drivability. What matters most are chassis and bulkhead integrity, verifiable import and title paperwork, a confirmed California registration path, and evidence that the drivetrain work was actually done. Fresh paint and accessories count for little.
profiles.weak_points: ['Chassis corrosion. The ladder frame rusts from the inside out. Worst areas are the rear crossmember, the rear spring hangers and trailing-arm mounts, the outriggers (especially the bulkhead outriggers below the A-pillars), and the gearbox crossmember area. Fresh underseal or black paint on a recently imported truck is a red flag until probed with a hammer or screwdriver. A rear crossmember replacement runs about $800–2,000. Outrigger sections run $300–800 each. A full galvanized chassis swap is roughly $9,000–16,000 installed. Ask for dated underside photos taken before any undercoating.', 'Bulkhead (firewall) rot. The steel bulkhead rots at the footwells, the door-pillar bases, the top rail under the windscreen seal, and the vent flap channels. Water leaks and carpet or vinyl hide it, so pull the floor mats and inspect from underneath. Footwell and pillar-foot repair sections run about $1,500–4,000 per side done properly. A bulkhead replacement or full rebuild is $6,000–12,000 because it is effectively a body-off job.', 'Windscreen frame and door corrosion. The steel windscreen frame rots at the lower corners and hinge feet. The aluminum door skins blister and separate from their steel frames, and door bottoms rot out. Replacement doors and screen frames are common on these imports. Check fit, seals, and whether the parts are new or used. Budget about $400–1,200 for a screen frame and $600–1,500 per door including fitting.', 'Galvanic corrosion of the aluminum body. Look for white, chalky bubbling where the aluminum panels touch steel fixings, cappings, rivets, and hinges. It is cosmetic at first, but it signals how the truck was stored and how well any repaint was prepped. A shiny new gray paint job can hide active corrosion.', 'Engine originality and conversion quality. Otokar 110s commonly left the factory with naturally aspirated 2.5 diesel or 2.5 petrol engines. US examples often carry 200Tdi or 300Tdi swaps. Check the following: engine mounts, the correct bellhousing and gearbox match, intercooler and radiator sizing, throttle and kickdown linkage, fuel lift pump and filter plumbing, glow-plug wiring, and the tachometer drive. Stamp the engine number into your notes and match it to the receipts. Fixing a sloppy conversion can easily cost $1,500–5,000.', "200Tdi and 300Tdi engine maintenance. The timing belt has a roughly 60k-mile / 5-year interval, about $600–1,200 with tensioner, idler, and front seal. A belt failure on these interference-adjacent engines can bend valves. Watch for head gasket weeping or cracking from past overheating ($1,500–3,000). Check the Bosch VE injection pump for weeps and the turbo for oil seal leaks and shaft play ($900–1,800 for a turbo). 'Turned-up' fueling (an adjusted boost pin or fuel screw) produces black smoke and high exhaust temperatures. Ask for the timing belt date, any rebuild invoice with a machine-shop line, and a compression or leakdown result.", "LT77 5-speed gearbox (pre-1994 R380). The LT77 is the weakest drivetrain link. Symptoms are input shaft and clutch spline wear causing driveline clunk, weak 2nd and 3rd synchros, 5th gear wear (it jumps out or whines), and pop-out under load. Check whether it carries an earlier or later suffix. A rebuild runs about $2,000–3,500. An R380 swap runs $3,500–6,000. Look for a rebuild invoice with parts listed, not just the word 'rebuilt'.", 'LT230 transfer case and center diff lock. Watch for the diff lock failing to engage or disengage, a sticking diff-lock warning switch, and oil leaks from the output seals. Brake-drum transmission-handbrake contamination from leaking seals is common. Low-range engagement can be stiff. Seal and bearing work runs about $500–1,500. Center diff wear shows up as a driveline clunk and is more expensive.', 'Front swivel hubs and CV joints. Pitted chrome swivel balls tear the seals, leaking EP90 or one-shot grease onto the brakes. Swivel preload goes out of spec, causing steering wander and shimmy. Worn Birfi

profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Swivel hub rebuild (chrome balls, seals, bearings) on one or both sides', 'Radius arm, panhard rod, and trailing link bush replacement; new shocks if they are original or unknown', 'Clutch, release bearing, and slave cylinder replacement if engagement is high or the clutch slips; check the LT77 input spline at the same time', 'Brake flexible hoses, and calipers or wheel cylinders as needed', 'Water leak remediation: door seals, alpine window seals, windscreen seal, roof seals', 'Rust repair on any outrigger, rear crossmember, or footwell sections found at inspection', 'Injection pump seal kit or turbo service if weeps or oil seepage appear', 'Exhaust hangers and joints, and intercooler hose and clamp replacement']
profiles.market_notes: Otokar-built trucks trade below equivalent Solihull-built 110s, and naturally aspirated examples trade below Tdi-converted ones. A documented 200Tdi or 300Tdi swap, especially paired with an R380, adds real value. Verified chassis condition matters most: a documented galvanized chassis or a solid original chassis with underside photos is worth thousands. 5-door station wagons with full glass and rear seating outsell hardtops and pickups. Clean US title, complete import paperwork, and LHD all support price. Heavy accessorizing (winch, bars, lights) adds little and can hide problems. Fresh cosmetic refreshes on recent Turkish imports are common and should not be priced as restorations. Kilometer readings are largely meaningless, so price on condition and documentation, not odometer.
profiles.catchup_notes: Assume a 30+ year-old recent import needs every fluid changed, a timing belt, swivel and bush work, brake hoses, and a wiring cleanup, regardless of 'refurbished' claims. Budget roughly $3,000–6,000 for catch-up on a decent example. Hidden chassis or bulkhead rot is the swing factor that can add $5,000–15,000.

profiles.label: Land Rover LR4 / Discovery 4 (L319, 2010–2016, incl. HSE Lux & Landmark)
profiles.framing: For this buyer the LR4 is a genuinely capable, seven-seat family and Central Coast adventure wagon: Terrain Response, twin-speed transfer case, air suspension and real ground clearance in a package that still rides like a luxury car on Highway 1. It is not an investment and should never be bought as one — final-year 2016 Landmark cars have a modest collector halo, but running costs behave like a used luxury SUV with a hand-built British electrical system. What matters is documentation of the expensive stuff (timing chain hardware on the AJ126 supercharged V6, coolant pipes, air suspension, differentials) and a car that has been serviced by a specialist rather than deferred. Buy the best-documented example, not the cheapest, and budget a real reserve from day one.
profiles.weak_points:
1) AJ126 3.0 supercharged V6 timing chain and tensioner wear (2014–2016 cars, and the related AJ133 5.0 V8 chain issue on 2010–2013): a cold-start rattle of 1–3 seconds, chain stretch codes (P0016/P0017/P0018), or a whirring/ticking at idle points to guides and hydraulic tensioners. Failure is catastrophic (valve-to-piston contact). Preventive chain service is engine-out or front-cover-off labor, roughly $6,000–$10,000 at an independent, more at a dealer. Ask for a cold-start video with sound and any chain/tensioner invoices; unrecorded 90k+ cars carry this risk unpriced.
2) Plastic coolant crossover pipes / thermostat housing / water pump on the 3.0 SC: the OEM composite pipes under the supercharger go brittle with heat cycles and can split without warning, dumping coolant and risking overheat damage to an aluminum engine. Aftermarket billet-aluminum pipe upgrade kits exist and are the tell of a knowledgeable owner; expect $1,200–$2,500 done with the water pump and thermostat while access is open. Look for a receipt naming 'coolant crossover pipes,' 'aluminum pipe upgrade,' or supercharger removal.
3) Supercharger nose-cone bearings and the isolator/coupler: a whine changing pitch or a rattle at idle around 80–120k miles. Nose cone rebuild $600–$1,200; whole blower far more.
4) Air suspension: EAS compressor (Hitachi/AMK) and dryer wear out around 80–130k miles, symptoms are slow rise, 'Suspension Fault' messages, a car that sits low overnight, or a compressor that runs long and hot. Compressor with dryer $600–$1,400 installed; individual air springs $350–$700 each; valve block and height sensors add up. Coil-spring conversions are a red flag on a car this buyer wants unmodified.
5) Cooling-system periphery generally: expansion tank cracks, radiator and intercooler-circuit auxiliary pump, and the low-temp radiator on SC cars. A one-time overheat event can cook the engine — check for coolant staining in the vee and Carfax/dealer notes of 'overheating.'
6) Rear differential and driveshaft: rear diff bearing whine and pinion seal leaks appear from ~90k; center support bearing and rear driveshaft U-joints/flex disc cause a 40–60 mph vibration or clunk on throttle transitions. Driveshaft $700–$1,400, rear diff rebuild/replace $1,800–$3,500.
7) Front suspension wear items: lower control arm bushings and ball joints, plus front upper arms — typical at 70–110k, causing a shimmy over the mid-corner ruts on local backroads. All four arms $1,200–$2,000; alignment mandatory after air-suspension or arm work.
8) Sunroof and body drains: the triple-sunroof cars (Landmark, HSE Lux) plug drains and wet the headliner, A-pillars and, worse, the passenger footwell and front SRS/BCM connectors — check for damp carpet padding and musty smell. Also alpine window seals and tailgate/upper-glass hinge corrosion.
9) Electrical gremlins and parasitic drain: a weak battery causes cascading warning lights (park brake, suspension, transmission fault). Electric parking brake actuator module failure ($700–$1,200), HVAC blend-door actuators, front and rear camera/infotainment modules, and door-latch/window regulator faults are common. Always test every module cold and hot.
10) In-tank fuel pump / low-pressure fuel supply failures on the SC V6 (this generation has documented pump replacements around 60–90k, ~$900–$1,600) plus high-pressure pump and injector issues showing as long crank or misfire under load.
11) Oil leaks: cam cover gaskets, oil cooler/filter housing, and the timing cover on high-mile motors — usually $500–$1,500 each depending on access; a soaked engine bay masks the more serious coolant leaks.
12) Transmission: the ZF 8HP is strong but was 'filled for life.' A 98k car with no fluid service should get a pan/filter/fluid change ($500–$800); look for shudder at light throttle 1,200–1,600 rpm (torque converter lock-up) and harsh 2-3 shifts.
13) Brakes and tires: heavy vehicle, front rotors/pads every 30–40k ($900–$1,400 axle set with rotors); 20
profiles.immediate_repairs: Full fluid catch-up (engine oil, ZF 8HP pan/filter/fluid if undocumented, front/rear diff and transfer case fluid, brake fluid, coolant condition test); four matching tires if the set is mixed or aged; new AGM battery unless dated within ~3 years; air-suspension full-cycle test and likely compressor/dryer service; clear all stored fault codes and re-scan after a 100-mile shakedown; clean all four sunroof and A-pillar drains; front brake pads/rotors if under 4mm; correct any cam-cover or oil-cooler seepage. Expect $2,500–$5,000 on a typical 90–100k example.
profiles.repairs_12mo: Coolant crossover pipe upgrade with water pump and thermostat if not already documented ($1,200–$2,500); front lower control arm bushings/ball joints and alignment ($1,200–$2,000); air spring(s) or valve block as leaks appear ($400–$1,500); supercharger nose-cone bearing or isolator if whining ($600–$1,200); rear driveshaft center bearing/flex disc or rear diff seals ($700–$1,800); HVAC actuator, parking-brake module or camera/infotainment module repair ($400–$1,200); spark plugs and both drive belts if not stamped. Timing-chain service is the big contingency if any cold-start rattle or chain codes appear.
profiles.market_notes: Price is driven first by service documentation — a folder showing coolant pipes, chain hardware, air suspension and transmission service is worth several thousand dollars over an equal-mileage mystery car. Final-year 2016 cars, especially the Landmark and HSE Lux with three sunroofs, Meridian, surround cameras and the HD/heavy-duty package (full-size matching spare, locking rear diff), carry a premium; missing HD pack and mismatched 20" tires are cheapening details. Sub-80k-mile examples and desirable color combos (Santorini Black, Fuji White, Corris Grey over Ebony) bring the strongest money, while any Carfax damage entries, unrepaired suspension faults, or coil-spring conversions produce steep discounts. Regional bidding for these on BaT clusters $18k–$32k depending on miles and records, with hollow-market risk below $15k where the buyer inherits every deferred item.
profiles.catchup_notes: A typical 90–100k mile LR4 arrives with life-of-vehicle fluids never changed, an aging battery causing phantom faults, a tired air-suspension compressor and original coolant pipes. Plan on a comprehensive fluid and consumables catch-up plus air-suspension and cooling-system attention in the first year, and treat undocumented timing-chain hardware as an open $6k–$10k liability rather than a solved problem.

profiles.label: Land Rover Range Rover Classic (US-market 1987–1995)
profiles.framing: For a Carmel-based buyer, a Range Rover Classic is a characterful, upright, genuinely capable 4x4 for coast and Carmel Valley use. It should be bought as an old British truck that needs ongoing care, not as a turnkey commuter. Condition matters most in two places: the steel structure hidden under the aluminum skins, and the health of the Rover V8's cooling system and head gaskets. Paint, interior and gadgets come a distant second. A documented, unmodified, rust-controlled example with a clean California smog history is worth a real premium over a cheaper truck that needs structural or engine work.
profiles.weak_points: ["Structural rust under aluminum panels. The outer skins are aluminum, but the inner structure and chassis are steel. Rust forms where the two metals meet and where water collects. Typical spots: the rear load floor and its supports, the inner and outer sills, the front footwells and bulkhead corners below the windscreen, the B/C-pillar bases, the lower tailgate frame and the upper tailgate glass frame. On the chassis, check the rear crossmember, the rear spring/shock towers, the outriggers and the radius-arm mounts. A fresh undercoat or 'rust inhibitor' spray can hide rot. Ask for pre-coating photos and probe the metal during inspection. Small patch work runs $1,500–4,000. Sill, floor or chassis rail repair runs $5,000–15,000 or more and can make a driver-grade truck uneconomic.", 'Rover 3.9L (and 4.2L LWB) V8 cooling and head gaskets. These alloy engines punish overheating. The usual failure chain is a clogged radiator, a weak viscous fan clutch, a failing water pump, or an air lock after amateur coolant work. The results are blown head gaskets or warped heads, and occasionally liner movement or cracked blocks. Warning signs: coolant loss with no visible leak, a pressurized overflow tank, mayonnaise on the oil cap, white exhaust smoke, or a temperature gauge that creeps on climbs. A head gasket job runs about $2,500–4,000. A rebuilt or exchange engine runs $8,000–15,000. Look for receipts covering the radiator, water pump, fan clutch, hoses and any previous head work.', 'Rover V8 lubrication and timing wear. The flat-tappet cam and lifters wear, especially on modern low-zinc oil, and show up as tapping lifters. The timing chain stretches and the cam gear wears; replacement runs about $800–1,500. The front cover and oil pump wear, causing low hot-idle oil pressure. Oil leaks are chronic at the rear main seal, the rocker covers, the timing cover and the oil cooler lines. Ask for oil-change intervals and the oil type used. At high mileage, budget for a leak-down test.', 'Lucas 14CUX fuel injection and ignition. Common faults: vacuum leaks from brittle hoses and the plenum gasket, failing hot-wire airflow meters ($300–700), idle stepper motor problems, and fuel pressure regulator faults. Also check for degraded in-tank fuel pump hoses, which cause stalling and are a fire risk; fuel pump work runs $400–900. Ignition faults come from the distributor cap, rotor, plug leads and amplifier. Symptoms are hunting idle, hesitation, hot-start problems and failed smog tests. Ask for fault code readouts and a smog report showing the HC, CO and NOx numbers.', "ZF 4HP22/4HP24 automatic transmission. These units are adequate but stressed by the truck's weight, towing, and fluid neglect. Watch for delayed engagement into Drive or Reverse, a slipping or flared 2–3 shift, harsh downshifts, and dark or burnt fluid. Cooler line leaks at the radiator are also common. A rebuild runs about $3,000–5,000 installed. Ask for fluid and filter service records. Heavy towing history, suggested by a receiver hitch, deserves extra scrutiny.", 'Transfer case and viscous coupling. US trucks from 1989 use the LT230 gear-drive transfer case with a viscous coupling in the center differential. Early 1987–88 trucks use the Borg-Warner chain-drive case. When the coupling seizes, the drivetrain binds on tight turns, scrubs tires and makes clunks. Mismatched tire sizes or tread depths accelerate this. A coupling replacement runs $700–1,500. Also check for output seal leaks, worn transfer case mounts, and the low-range shift. Do a tight-circle test on pavement.', 'Rover axles and swivel housings. Pitted chrome swivel balls tear their seals, leaking oil onto the brakes and letting grit into the CV joints. Other wear items are the swivel pin bearings, wheel bearings and pinion seals. A swivel rebuild runs $800–1,600 per side. Propshaft U-joints and the double-cardan front shaft are wear items at about $300–700 each. Look for oil-wet swivels and clunks on drive engagement.',
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Full fluid service: engine oil and filter (high-zinc or flat-tappet-appropriate oil), ZF transmission fluid and filter, LT230 transfer case oil, front and rear differential oil, swivel housing oil or grease, power steering fluid', 'Cooling system refresh: flush, new thermostat, all rubber hoses, coolant reservoir cap, and inspection of the radiator, water pump and viscous fan clutch, with replacement as needed', 'Brake fluid flush with ABS accumulator and pump test, pads and rotors as needed, rubber brake hoses if original or cracked', 'Ignition and vacuum tune: distributor cap, rotor, plugs and leads, plus all vacuum and breather hoses, to stabilize idle and pass smog', 'Fuel system inspection: in-tank hoses, filter and pressure regulator; replace degraded fuel hoses immediately for fir
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Swivel ball and seal rebuild on one or both sides if leaking or pitted', 'Suspension bushing refresh: radius arms, Panhard rod, trailing links, plus shocks and the steering damper', 'Steering box reseal or adjustment if play or leaks are present', 'Propshaft U-joints and transfer case output seals', 'A/C system repair or proper R-134a conversion, including any evaporator, condenser, compressor or hose work', 'Exhaust manifold gaskets or studs and heat shield securing', 'Headliner re-cover and minor interior repairs (seat heaters, bolsters)', 'Electrical fixes: door lock actuators, window regulators, headlamp washer pump, gauge senders', 'Tailgate frame and localized rust repair before it progresses', 'Timing chain and gears, if high mileage with no record of replacement']
profiles.market_notes: Structural condition dominates price. A rust-controlled truck with a dry California or Southwest history and documented chassis, sills and tailgate commands a large premium over one with hidden rot. Late County LWB (1993–95, 4.2L, air suspension) and 1995 soft-dash County Classic trucks bring the most, followed by well-kept 3.9L County models, with desirable original colors such as Beluga Black, Alpine White, Portofino Red and Windsor Green helping. High-mileage driver-quality trucks with deferred A/C, cosmetic or rust issues trade roughly $10k–20k. Well-documented, sorted, unmodified examples bring $25k–45k, and restored or resto-mod trucks are a separate market well above that. Thick service files covering head gaskets, cooling, transmission and rust repair move price more than mileage. Aftermarket stereos, headlights and exhausts are mild negatives for originality-focused buyers.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most surviving trucks have 25–35 years of deferred rubber and fluids. Plan on replacing coolant and fuel hoses, bushings, brake hoses and seals, and on servicing every driveline fluid, before trusting the truck on longer drives. Also expect to address active corrosion at the steel/aluminum interfaces and to properly repair the A/C rather than recharge it, which typically adds $3,000–7,000 of catch-up work beyond the purchase price.

profiles.label: Land Rover Range Rover Sport SVR (L494, 2015-2022)
profiles.framing: For a Carmel-based driver, the SVR is a fast, comfortable SUV that handles Highway 1 and Carmel Valley roads well and still manages light trail or beach-access duty. It is not a reliable appliance. It is an aluminum-bodied, air-sprung, supercharged 5.0L AJ133 V8 with heavy electronics, and depreciation has made the purchase price the cheap part. What matters most is a clean, verifiable history across both Carfax and AutoCheck, proof of coolant-system and air-suspension health, a clean full-module scan, and an underbody free of serious corrosion. Budget the car as a high-running-cost luxury vehicle with a real repair reserve.
profiles.weak_points: ["Coolant system leaks are the signature AJ133 5.0 SC problem and the most common big bill. Typical failure points: the plastic coolant pipes and crossover in the engine valley/rear of the block, the water pump, the thermostat housing, heater hose quick-connect fittings, and cracked expansion tanks. They typically show up from about 40-70k miles or 5+ years. Symptoms are a sweet smell, pink/white crust on the valley, timing cover or bellhousing, low-coolant warnings, and overheating on long climbs. Repair runs $800-1,500 for a water pump or thermostat. Valley pipe work, which requires removing the supercharger, runs $2,500-4,500. Look for receipts naming the specific parts replaced, not just 'coolant leak repaired'.", "The supercharger's separate intercooler coolant circuit has its own failure points: the electric auxiliary pump, hoses, and the intercooler bricks themselves. A failing pump shows as heat-soak power loss, limp mode, or codes for the charge-air cooler pump. Pumps cost $400-900 installed. Intercooler or brick replacement with supercharger removal costs $2,500-5,000.", 'The supercharger drive coupler/isolator (the damper between pulley snout and rotors) wears and produces a rattle or marble-like clatter at idle, often 50-80k miles. The repair is $900-1,800 because the supercharger must come off. Doing it alongside valley coolant pipe work saves labor.', 'Timing chain tensioners, guides, and cam phasers were a major issue on early 2010-2013 AJ133 engines. Updated parts make this less common on SVRs, but heavy oil-change-interval abuse still causes stretch. Watch for cam/crank correlation codes P0016-P0019, P0008/P0009, or a startup rattle. A full chain, guide, and tensioner job runs $4,500-8,000. Oil change records at 7,500-10,000 mile intervals or less, using the JLR-spec 0W-20, matter.', 'Oil leaks are common with age. Typical sources: valve cover gaskets, front timing cover, oil cooler/oil filter housing seals, and the rear crankshaft seal. Cam cover gaskets run $900-1,800. A timing cover reseal is $2,500+. Check for oil on the exhaust manifolds (burning smell) and on the undertray.', "The air suspension needs inspection on every car: front and rear air struts (bag perishing and top-mount leaks), the compressor (which wears out from chasing leaks), the valve block, and height sensors. Symptoms are a sag overnight, 'Suspension Fault' messages, slow raising, or a compressor running constantly. Costs: compressor $1,000-1,800, a single strut $1,200-2,500 dealer (less with quality aftermarket), valve block $600-1,200. Plan for at least one air suspension repair by 60-90k miles.", 'The front lower control arm rear bushings and ball joints wear early on this heavy SUV, especially on 22-inch wheels. Symptoms are clunks over bumps, braking shimmy, uneven inner tire wear, and repeated alignments. Arms cost $800-2,000 per axle. Wheel bearings and tie-rod ends also wear faster on 22s. Frequent tire replacement or alignment entries in the history are a clue.', 'SVR brakes are large Brembo 6-piston fronts with big rotors. Some later cars have optional carbon-ceramics. Steel rotors and pads cost $1,800-3,500 per full set at an independent shop, more at the dealer. Carbon-ceramic rotors are $10k+ per axle if worn, so get a rotor thickness and lip measurement. Pedal pulsation means warped rotors.', "The ZF 8HP70 automatic is robust but sold as 'lifetime fill'. Expect harsh 1-2 or 2-3 shifts, flare, and mechatronic sleeve or pan leaks by 60-100k miles. A fluid, pan, and filter service runs $600-1,000. A mechatronic unit runs $2,500-4,500. The active rear locking differential and transfer case leak and have actuator faults. Fluid services are cheap ($250-500), but an e-diff actuator or unit runs $1,500-4,000.", "Electrical and electronics problems are common: battery drain and Intelligent Battery Sensor faults, intermittent warnings, and parking sensor and camera failures. Infotainment reboots or blank screens affect both InControl

profiles.market_notes: Pre-facelift 2015-2017 cars (550 hp, older InControl) trade below 2018+ facelift cars (575 hp, Touch Pro Duo, Pivi upgrades, revised styling). Carbon packs, carbon-ceramic brakes, and the 2022 Carbon/Ultimate Editions command a premium. Clean single-source history, US-market provenance, low miles (under 40k), and an existing transferable warranty or CPO coverage add meaningful value. Canadian-origin cars, any accident entry (especially 'severe' or structural), conflicting Carfax and AutoCheck reports, and salt-belt corrosion bring steep discounts that are well deserved. Heavy depreciation means a well-documented $35-50k example is often cheaper to own than a $25-30k car with a cloudy past.
profiles.catchup_notes: A typical 2018-2019 example at 50-60k miles is entering its first major-maintenance window. Expect spark plugs, transmission fluid, brakes, tires, and a likely coolant-system or air-suspension repair within the first year, often totaling $4,000-8,000 on top of routine service. Salt-belt or Canadian cars add seized-hardware labor and corrosion treatment, and a new transferable warranty does not cover these wear items.
