profiles.label: Mercedes-Benz SL-Class R107 (350SL/450SL/380SL/560SL, 1971-1989)
profiles.framing: The R107 is a heavy, overbuilt two-seat convertible for top-down cruising on Highway 1 and Carmel Valley Road, not a sports car. It is simple enough for an independent shop to keep on the road. The price is set almost entirely by structural rust, the health of the timing chain and fuel injection, and whether the car passes California smog. US cars were automatic-only, so an automatic is normal here and not a compromise. A 1979 450SL at the bottom of the market is only a bargain if the floors, sills and chain guides check out, because body rot and a jumped chain can each cost more than the car.
profiles.weak_points: ['Structural rust is the number-one killer. Inspect the rocker panels, the four jacking points, the front and rear floor pans (especially under the carpets behind the seats), the rear wheel-arch lips, and the trunk floor and spare-tire well. Also check the lower windshield frame and A-pillar bases, where the cowl and windshield seal leak. Bubbles under the chrome trim and around the headlight buckets usually mean far worse underneath. Proper metal repair on sills and floors runs $3,000-10,000+. Look for underbody photos from a lift and ask whether the carpets have ever been pulled.', 'Clogged soft-top well and cowl drains send water into the cabin and trunk. Wet or musty carpets, rusty seat-rail bolts and a water line in the spare-tire well are warning signs of hidden floor rot.', 'Timing chain guide rails (M117 V8) become brittle with age and break regardless of mileage. Pieces can drop into the oil pan, and the chain can jump and bend valves. Guides, tensioner and chain cost roughly $1,200-3,000; valve damage pushes a repair to $4,000-7,000. Ask for dated receipts for guides and chain, ideally within the last 60k miles or 15 years. If there are none, budget for the job immediately. On 1981-83 380SLs, also confirm the original single-row chain was converted to double-row.', 'Camshaft lobe and rocker-arm wear is common on 4.5 and 3.8 V8s, often from oil spray-bar problems or long oil-change intervals. Symptoms are ticking at idle and lost power. Cams and rockers run about $2,000-4,000. Look for oil-change records and ask whether anyone has inspected the cams with the valve covers off.', 'Valve stem seals harden with age and cause a puff of blue smoke on a cold start or after idling. Replacing them with the heads on the engine costs about $900-1,800. Watch the cold start in person or on video.', 'The Bosch K-Jetronic (CIS) mechanical fuel injection (1976-on US cars; 1972-75 used D-Jetronic) causes hard hot starts, cold-start stumble and poor idle. The usual culprits are the warm-up regulator, cold-start valve, fuel accumulator, fuel pump, fuel distributor, injector seals and vacuum leaks. Rust from a tank that sat unused contaminates the whole system. Baseline tuning costs $300-800; a distributor, regulator or accumulator can reach $1,500-3,000. Look for fuel-system receipts and a smog printout showing emissions numbers.', 'California smog applies. Model-year 1976 and newer cars are not exempt, and the seller must supply a smog certificate that is less than 90 days old. Missing or rusted catalytic converters, air-injection pumps and vacuum-controlled emissions parts, plus a rich-running CIS, cause failures. Emissions repairs typically run $500-2,500 and can be more if a CARB-legal catalytic converter is needed.', 'The three-speed automatic has several known faults. A leaking vacuum modulator pulls transmission fluid into the intake, causing smoke and low fluid. Other symptoms of wear are harsh or late shifts, slipping, and delayed engagement. A rebuild costs $2,500-4,500. Check that the fluid is red and not burnt, and look for any service history.', 'Driveline rubber ages out. The driveshaft flex discs, center support bearing, and engine and transmission mounts deteriorate, causing clunks when shifting into gear and vibration at speed. Expect $400-1,200.', 'Front-end wear shows up as wander and a loose steering feel. The usual causes are front lower ball joints, upper and lower control-arm bushings, the idler-arm bushing, tie rods, the steering damper, play in the steering box, and rear subframe and trailing-arm bushings. Suspension refreshes run $800-3,000.', 'Cooling-system age can overheat these heavy V8s in inland heat. Weak points are the original radiator (plastic tanks on later cars), water pump, viscous fan clutch and hoses. Expect $500-1,500. Look for a steady temperature gauge and a history of coolant service.', 'Electrical and instrument faults are common. The ceramic fuse box corrodes, and window motors and regulato
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Full fluid service: engine oil and filter, transmission fluid and filter, differential oil, power-steering fluid, coolant flush, and brake fluid flush', 'Fuel filter replacement plus a CIS baseline: fuel pressure test, warm-up regulator and cold-start valve check, vacuum-leak smoke test, and idle/mixture set', 'Timing chain, guide and tensioner inspection with the valve covers off (and replacement if there are no receipts)', 'Belts, radiator and heater hoses, and vacuum lines', 'Tires by date code (anything over 6-7 years old gets replaced regardless of tread)', 'Brake inspection: caliper function, rubber hoses, and pad and rotor condition', 'Clearing the soft-top well and cowl drains, and checking the trunk and floors for standing water', 'Inspection of the driveshaft flex discs, center
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Front-end refresh: ball joints, control-arm bushings, idler arm, tie rods and steering damper', 'Valve stem seals if the car smokes on startup', 'Engine and transmission mounts plus the driveshaft flex discs', 'Cooling-system refresh: radiator, water pump and fan clutch as needed', 'Soft-top replacement or pad and weatherstrip renewal', 'CIS parts as needed: accumulator, fuel pump, injector seals and warm-up regulator', 'A/C repair or R134a conversion, plus vacuum-actuator repair for climate and central locking', 'Speedometer and odometer gear repair', 'Door, window and hardtop weatherseals']
profiles.market_notes: The 560SL (1986-89) commands the highest prices, especially with low miles, followed by the 380SL. The US 450SL, especially 1976-80 CIS cars with smaller bumpers, is the cheapest entry point. Rough examples trade at $6,000-10,000, good drivers at $12,000-20,000, and exceptional documented cars well above that. A rust-free California history, the factory hardtop, a good soft top, working A/C and a thick folder of records move price the most. Silver, red, black and white with black or tan interiors sell better than 1970s greens and browns. Mileage matters less than documentation because odometers often fail. Aftermarket wheels, European-style bumper conversions or removed emissions equipment reduce value and can make smog compliance impossible.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most R107s have spent decades with sporadic use, so expect to renew essentially all rubber: hoses, mounts, bushings, flex discs, seals and tires. Also expect to baseline the CIS system and address timing chain guides that are brittle with age even at modest miles. Budget $3,000-6,000 of catch-up on a typical driver-grade car before counting any rust, top or transmission work.

profiles.label: Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren (C199/R199 Coupe, Roadster, 722 Edition, 722 S, Stirling Moss; 2004–2010)
profiles.framing: The SLR is a hand-built, carbon-tub, front-mid-engine supercharged GT made by McLaren in Woking under Mercedes badging. It is a brutally fast but civil long-distance car that suits Highway 1, Carmel Valley Road and Monterey Car Week use, with a low nose and a wide body to manage on steep driveways. Every US car is an automatic. For a driver-focused buyer, what matters most is how the car has been stored and woken up after long periods of sitting. Key items are the SBC brake system, carbon-ceramic rotor life, tire age, transmission connector leaks, door strut and air-brake function, and access to an SLR-trained Mercedes dealer with current Xentry diagnostics. Low miles on these cars usually mean deferred age-related work rather than freshness.
profiles.weak_points: ["Sensotronic Brake Control (SBC): The SLR uses Mercedes' electro-hydraulic brake-by-wire system. The hydraulic unit has an internal pump with a usage counter and stored fault memory. Symptoms of trouble include 'Brake Visit Workshop' or SBC warnings, a hard or inconsistent pedal, and audible pump cycling. Long storage and low battery voltage provoke faults. A replacement unit plus Xentry programming and bleeding typically runs $4,000–$10,000 at a dealer. Ask for a Xentry printout showing SBC fault memory and counter status, and confirm by VIN with Mercedes whether any SBC campaign or warranty extension applies.", 'Carbon-ceramic brake rotors and pads: The rotors are long-lived on street cars, but they wear by oxidation and mass loss, not just thickness. They also chip at the edges and crack from the cross-drill holes after hard track use or corrosion. Replacement is a five-figure job: roughly $15,000–$30,000+ per axle with pads, depending on parts availability. Ask for a dealer rotor inspection or weight measurement, and photos of rotor faces and edges.', 'Tires: Many low-mile SLRs still wear original or decade-old tires (staggered 19-inch, 245 front / 295 rear). Rubber over 6 years old is a safety issue on a 617-hp RWD car, regardless of tread depth. Budget $2,000–$3,500 mounted. Read the DOT date codes on all four tires before bidding.', 'Transmission (5-speed AMG Speedshift R, based on the 722.6): The internal electrical connector and pin bushing seep ATF into the harness. Left untreated, this can wick fluid toward the TCU and cause harsh or limp-mode shifts. Conductor plate and speed-sensor faults also occur. The bushing is a $300–$800 job; a conductor plate or valve body runs $1,500–$4,000. Ask for records of connector repair and ATF/filter service dates, which are often overdue on low-mile cars.', 'M155 5.4L supercharged V8 intercooler circuit: The electric intercooler (aftercooler) pump fails with age. Symptoms are heat-soak power loss, then fault codes. Expect $800–$2,000 including bleeding. Low coolant in the separate intercooler circuit is a related tell.', "M155 vacuum lines, breather hoses and crankcase ventilation: Age-hardened rubber and plastic connectors crack, causing rough idle, lean codes, and air-brake or HVAC vacuum faults. The example listing's vacuum three-way connector replacement is typical. Individual fixes are cheap ($200–$1,500), but access is labor-heavy.", 'Engine oil leaks and dry-sump specifics: Valve cover gaskets, oil cooler lines and dry-sump tank fittings weep with age. The harmonic balancer and engine mounts on this M113K-derived family can deteriorate. Oil level must be checked using the dry-sump procedure. Typical costs: gaskets $1,000–$2,500; harmonic balancer $1,500–$3,000.', "Swing-wing (butterfly) door gas struts and hinges: Struts weaken over time, so doors won't stay up, drift, or slam. Hinge wear and misalignment cause wind noise, seal damage and water leaks. Strut replacement runs $1,000–$3,000 per pair installed. Test each door's full open, hold and close cycle, in cold and warm conditions if possible.", 'Active rear air-brake spoiler: The hydraulic or electric actuation leaks, sticks or throws faults. It should raise under hard braking at speed and can be cycled from the console. Actuator or pump repairs run $3,000–$12,000+ depending on parts sourcing. Ask for a video or demonstration of the full raise/lower cycle, and check for fluid residue under the decklid.', 'Electrical system and batteries: The SLR is very sensitive to low voltage, and storage without a maintainer creates cascades of SBC, cluster, TPMS and door/convenience faults. The example listing shows batteries replaced plus cluster and TPMS reprogramming, which is a common pattern. Expect $500–$1,500 for batteries and coding. Ask whether the car was kept on a CTEK-type maintainer.', 'Carbon fiber tub and crash structures, front underbody: The car is low-slung with a long nose. Splitters, undertrays and front crash s
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Replace tires if any DOT date code is over about 6 years old, even with good tread', 'Brake fluid flush via Xentry SBC bleed procedure (on a 20-year-old car, a 2-year interval is essential)', 'Full Xentry quick test, clearing and documenting all faults (SBC, TCU, ME, cluster, door/spoiler modules)', 'A- or B-service if the last one is over 12 months old: oil using the dry-sump check procedure, filters, inspection', 'Transmission fluid and filter service, plus inspection of the electrical connector bushing for ATF seepage if not documented recently', 'Coolant service for both the main and intercooler circuits if the interval is unknown', 'Install a battery maintainer and verify charging-system health', 'Function-test both door struts and the air-brake spoiler, and address any marginal com
profiles.repairs_12mo: ["Door gas strut replacement (pair) if doors don't hold firmly", 'Intercooler pump replacement as preventive or condition-based work', 'Vacuum and breather hose refresh on the M155', 'Valve cover gaskets and oil cooler line seals if weeping', 'Spark plugs (16 plugs) if not documented within the age interval', 'A/C service or compressor seals if output degrades', 'Engine and transmission mount inspection and replacement', 'Air-brake spoiler actuator service if slow or leaking', 'Rotor and pad re-measurement, plus budget planning if rotor mass is near the wear limit']
profiles.market_notes:
Body and edition drive price first. Standard Coupes are the baseline; Roadsters typically trade close to Coupes. The 722 Edition Coupe (650 hp, ~150 built) and 722 S Roadster carry large premiums, and the Stirling Moss (~75 built) is a separate collector market. Within a variant, the main price drivers are:
- Complete Mercedes/SLR-dealer service records
- No accident history
- Mileage under about 10k
- Fresh SBC, tires and fluids
- Rare colors or interior combinations, such as 300SL Red or non-silver paint
Crystal Laurite Silver over black or red is the most common spec. Cars on original tires with stale records, an incomplete key set, or open fault codes should be discounted by the cost of the catch-up work. All cars are automatics, so transmission choice is not a factor.
profiles.catchup_notes: A typical SLR has very low miles but 15–20 years of age, so expect to replace tires and refresh all fluids, including the SBC brake bleed via Xentry, transmission and both coolant circuits. Also plan on aged rubber vacuum and breather lines, batteries, and door struts. Budget roughly $8,000–$20,000 to bring a stale-records car current, before any rotor, SBC or spoiler hydraulic surprises.

profiles.label: Mercury Capri / Capri XR2 (Australian-built SA30, 1991-1994)
profiles.framing: The 1991-94 Capri was built by Ford Australia on Mazda 323 (BF-era) mechanicals. The XR2 adds the 132-hp turbocharged, intercooled Mazda B6T 1.6 DOHC, almost always with a 5-speed. For this buyer it is a cheap, light, fun top-down runabout for coastal roads, not an investment. What matters is a dry, rust-free tub, a healthy turbo engine with a known timing-belt history, a sound top, and good original suspension and trim. Capri-specific body, trim and suspension parts are scarce or unobtainable, so a complete, unmolested car is worth far more than a cheap project.
profiles.weak_points: ["Water intrusion and floor rust: leaking soft-top seals, windshield-header and door-glass seals, and clogged body drains let water into the footwells. That soaks the carpet and padding, then rusts the floor pans, seat-mount areas and the lower A-pillar and sill junction. Fogged gauges, mildew smell or rusty seat bolts are red flags. Floor-pan and sill repair runs $1,500-4,000+ and can exceed the car's value. Ask for photos of the underside, the footwells with carpet lifted, and the spare-tire well.", 'Convertible top and hardtop: the top fabric, rear window and frame pivots wear, and latches and weatherstrips shrink. Hardtops fade and their seals and mounting hardware go missing. An aftermarket top is roughly $400-800 for the part plus $400-800 to install. Capri-specific weatherstrip is hard to source, and a good used hardtop is scarce.', 'Timing belt and water pump on the B6T: the interval is 60k miles or about 7 years, and most cars are overdue by age even at low miles. Treat the belt as unknown without a dated receipt. Budget $500-900 for belt, tensioner, water pump, cam and crank seals, and the CAS O-ring.', "Crank pulley and keyway wear: B6-family engines of this era (compare the early 1.6 Miata 'short-nose' crank) can develop crank-pulley wobble from keyway wear. That shows up as a wobbling pulley, timing scatter or belt walk. Caught early it means pulley bolt and keyway service at $200-500. If neglected, it can mean a crankshaft or engine at $1,500-3,500.", 'Turbocharger and boost plumbing: the original turbo can suffer worn shaft seals (blue smoke on startup or decel, oily intercooler piping), shaft play, coked oil feed and return lines, and cracked boost or vacuum hoses that cause low or erratic boost. A rebuild or replacement runs $800-1,800. Hose refresh is $150-400. Look for any service records and an unmodified boost-control setup.', 'Oil leaks and cooling system: valve-cover gasket, cam seals, CAS O-ring and oil-pan leaks are common. The original radiator with plastic tanks, the heater hoses and the thermostat are age-expired, and overheating risks a head gasket ($1,200-2,000). A cooling refresh is $400-800.', 'Clutch hydraulics and clutch: master and slave cylinders weep with age, and the turbo torque wears clutches, especially if previous owners abused it. A clutch job runs $800-1,300 and hydraulics $250-500. Watch for slipping in 3rd and 4th under boost, or a high, soft or sinking pedal.', 'Transaxle and driveline: worn 2nd and 3rd synchros (grinding on fast shifts) and sloppy shift-linkage bushings are common. Torn CV boots lead to clicking outer CV joints. Bushings and CV axles run $200-700. A used transaxle runs $800-1,500 installed.', 'Suspension parts scarcity: Capri-specific struts, strut mounts, springs and rear suspension bushings are hard or impossible to find new, and some cars have mismatched Mazda 323 or Festiva substitutes. Worn struts mean floaty, bouncy behavior or clunks. Good original suspension is a real plus, and sorting a tired setup can cost $600-1,500 plus parts hunting.', 'Electrical aging: pop-up headlight motors and linkages, slow power windows and tired regulators, and door-lock actuators all fail. Corroded grounds affect gauges and fuel-injection behavior. Original-style ECUs of this era can suffer leaking capacitors. Individual fixes run $100-500 each. A sorted car is worth a premium.', 'Air conditioning: the original R-12 system is likely leaking or empty. Recharging or converting to R-134a with a compressor, drier and seals runs $800-1,500, so many owners skip it.', 'Airbag and SRS (driver airbag wheel): a 30+-year-old airbag module, clockspring and crash sensors may set an SRS light. Parts are scarce, so note the warning-lamp status. Diagnosis and repair can cost $300-1,000 if parts are even available.', "Interior and trim plastics: brittle door handles, console and dash plastics crack and break. Seat fabric and bolsters wear, and Capri-unique badges, spoilers, lenses and side m

profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Clutch master and slave cylinders, and the clutch itself if slipping or high-engagement ($250-1,300)', 'Radiator, thermostat and cooling refresh ($400-800)', 'Valve-cover and oil-pan gasket reseal ($200-500)', 'CV axles or boots and shift-linkage bushings ($200-700)', 'Struts, mounts and bushings if available ($600-1,500)', 'Convertible top or rear window replacement if shrunk or leaking ($800-1,600 installed)', 'AC conversion or recharge if desired ($800-1,500)', 'Power window regulator and motor, plus pop-up headlight motor repairs ($150-600)', 'Turbo oil feed and return lines and boost-control check, or a turbo rebuild if smoking ($150-1,800)']
profiles.market_notes: These are inexpensive cars: driver XR2s commonly trade in the low-to-mid four figures, and only exceptionally clean, low-mile, documented examples push higher. The XR2 turbo with a 5-speed carries a clear premium over the base non-turbo or automatic Capri. A rust-free floor, an intact top, the original removable hardtop, and complete, uncracked Capri-specific trim and spoilers move price more than color does. Low documented mileage, timing-belt receipts and an unmodified engine add value, while rust, a missing hardtop, aftermarket modifications or missing trim cut it sharply because parts are so scarce.
profiles.catchup_notes: Even low-mile examples are 30+ years old, so assume all rubber is expired unless receipts prove otherwise: timing belt, hoses, seals, top weatherstrip, bushings and tires. Plan roughly $1,500-3,000 of catch-up work in the first year. Rust or a water-damaged interior can quickly push repair costs past the car's market value.

profiles.label: Mitsubishi Pajero Evolution (V55W, 1997–1999)
profiles.framing: The Pajero Evolution is a roughly 2,500–2,700-unit Dakar homologation special. It uses the short-wheelbase second-generation Pajero shell with wide fender flares, Evo-only front and rear suspension (including an independent multi-link rear), and the 3.5L 6G74 MIVEC V6. For a Carmel-based driver it can be a fun, capable daily or weekend truck, but many of its body, aero and suspension parts are now scarce, and a federal 25-year-import RHD car may face a difficult or expensive California registration path. Confirm registration feasibility before chasing condition. What matters most is a documented timing belt, a healthy automatic or manual and 4WD system, rust-free frame rails and suspension mounts, intact Evo-specific panels, and a stock suspension rather than welded or fabricated mounts.
profiles.weak_points: ['6G74 timing belt (interference engine): the interval is about 100,000 km / 60,000 mi or 7–10 years. Freshly imported cars usually have no paper trail, and a snapped belt typically means bent valves and an engine that is hard to source. Look for a dated receipt or Japanese service sticker showing belt, hydraulic tensioner, idler/tensioner pulleys, water pump and cam/crank seals replaced together. Without it, budget $1,000–1,800 for immediate replacement.', 'MIVEC and oil-control issues: rocker/cam cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals leak, and oil can foul plugs and coils. Sludged or neglected oil can make the MIVEC switchover solenoid or oil-pressure switch misbehave, causing a flat mid-range or a check-engine light. Rear-bank plugs and coils need the intake plenum removed, so plug jobs are $400–800, and a gasket set with plugs is $800–1,500.', "Crank harmonic balancer and accessory drive: the 25-year-old balancer's rubber layer can separate (wobbling pulley, belt walking off). Idler bearings, the A/C compressor clutch and the alternator are also age items. Balancer: $250–600. Full accessory refresh: $500–1,200.", 'Cooling system: original-style radiators with plastic end tanks crack. Viscous fan clutches weaken, and heater and bypass hoses harden. Overheating a 6G74 risks head-gasket or head warp. Look for evidence of a radiator replacement and coolant service, and watch the temperature gauge under hill-climb load on Highway 1 or Carmel Valley grades. Radiator, hoses and fan clutch: $700–1,500.', 'Five-speed INVECS-II automatic (shared family with the later Montero V5A51): harsh or flared 2-3 shifts, delayed engagement, slipping when hot, or limp mode usually trace to burnt fluid, worn clutch packs or the solenoid/valve body. It needs Diamond SP-III type fluid and benefits from an external cooler in hot or towing use. A drain-and-fill is cheap. A rebuild or used-unit swap is $3,500–6,500 because Evo-specific calibration and parts lead time add cost. Five-speed manuals are rarer; check clutch engagement height and synchro crunch, and budget $1,800–3,000 for a clutch with flywheel resurfacing.', 'Super Select transfer case and front axle engagement: the center viscous coupling can stiffen, causing binding or tire scrub in 4H on tight turns. The vacuum-actuated front axle disconnect (solenoids, vacuum lines, actuator) fails, giving a flashing 4WD lamp or failure to engage 4H/4HLc/4LLc. Chain stretch shows as clunks. Vacuum system repairs are $200–700. A viscous coupling or transfer case overhaul is $1,500–3,500 if parts can be found.', 'Front and rear LSD differentials and independent rear: the limited-slip units need the correct gear oil with friction modifier. Chatter on turns or whine on lift-off means neglected or worn diffs. The independent rear uses CV axles, so torn boots or clicking joints are common on an aged truck. Fluid service: $200–350. CV axles or boots: $300–900 per side. A diff overhaul with LSD clutch packs is $1,500–3,000.', 'Evo-only suspension parts: the double-wishbone front and multi-link rear use unique arms, bushings, knuckles and dampers. Bushings crack and dampers fade with age, and many replacement parts are discontinued or must come from Japan. Aftermarket or fabricated mounts (welded shock brackets, auxiliary dampers, lifts) can stress mounting points and are a red flag for a stock-preferring buyer. Bushing and damper refresh: $1,500–4,000. Reversing fabricated modifications can exceed that if welding repairs are needed.', "Rust and structure: these are generally better than salted-US trucks, but snow-region Japanese cars rot. Check the built-in frame rails, rear suspension subframe and crossmember mounts, sills, floor pans, rear wheel arches behind the flares, and the tailgate base and hinges. The swing-out spare-carrier tailgate sags and cracks its hinge areas from the spare's weight. Demand underbody photos on a lift. Structural rust or bad prior welding is a walk-away issue given parts scar
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Timing belt, tensioner, idlers, water pump and cam/crank seals if not documented within 5 years or 60,000 mi', 'Full fluid baseline: engine oil and filter, ATF drain-and-fill (SP-III type) or manual gearbox oil, transfer case, front and rear LSD diff oil, coolant, brake fluid, power steering fluid', 'Spark plugs and inspection of coil packs (rear bank requires plenum removal); check and replace valve cover and plug tube gaskets if oiled', 'Inspect or replace radiator, hoses and thermostat if original or brittle', 'New tires if older than 6–7 years or mismatched (24-31-year-old cars often sit on old rubber)', 'Battery, terminals and charging system test; address any check-engine or ABS lights with a scan', 'Test 4WD engagement (4H, 4HLc, 4LLc) and fix vacuum lines and solenoids for the fr
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Suspension bushing refresh and Evo-correct dampers (sourcing from Japan can take months)', 'CV boots or axles front and rear', 'Power steering hoses or pump reseal', 'Engine and transmission mounts', 'ECU capacitor inspection or recap; O2 sensors if slow or failed', 'Harmonic balancer and accessory drive pulleys and belts', 'Brake caliper service, flexible brake hoses, rotors and pads', 'A/C system service (compressor clutch, seals, recharge)', 'Rust treatment and underbody cleaning and coating if any surface corrosion is found', 'Additional ATF drain-and-fills to refresh fluid; external transmission cooler if not fitted']
profiles.market_notes: Price is driven mainly by originality and provenance. Unmodified trucks with intact, uncracked Evo aero and flares, factory wheels and documented Japanese history (auction sheet, export certificate, service stamps) bring the strongest money. Modified trucks, especially those with fabricated suspension mounts, aftermarket wheels or replica body parts, sell at a discount. Five-speed manuals and low-km examples command a premium over the more common automatics, and high-km (200,000+ km) trucks sit in the lower band. Bonded or branded titles, missing import paperwork, rust and unresolved registration issues (especially for California buyers) depress value sharply.
profiles.catchup_notes: Expect a recently imported example to need a full baseline service: timing belt kit, all driveline fluids, cooling system, plugs and gaskets, tires and rubber bushings. Its Japanese service history is often thin or unverifiable. Budget extra time and money for parts sourcing from Japan, and for reversing any aftermarket modifications to return the truck to stock.

profiles.label: Mitsubishi Starion / Dodge-Plymouth-Chrysler Conquest (1st gen narrowbody, non-intercooled, 1983–1986)
profiles.framing: For this buyer, the early narrowbody Starion is an analog, characterful 1980s turbo coupe to drive and enjoy on Highway 1 and Carmel Valley Road. It is not an appreciating asset: narrowbody non-intercooled cars sit well below widebody ESI-R values. Its real risk is parts scarcity. ECI fuel-injection components, narrowbody body trim, glass and interior plastics are discontinued or hard to find, so a complete, unmodified, documented car is worth paying up for over a cheap project. The car is a 1983–86 model, so in California it needs a biennial smog check with a visual inspection of all emissions equipment. Out-of-state cars must pass before registration, and any non-original engine or intake part needs a CARB EO number.
profiles.weak_points: ['Turbocharger (Mitsubishi TD05) and its cooling history: 1983–84 cars left the factory with an oil-only-cooled turbo center section that cokes its bearings after hot shutdowns. Mitsubishi ran a dealer campaign retrofitting a water-cooled turbo kit. Look for the dealer campaign paperwork or a clearly visible coolant line to the center section. Symptoms of a tired turbo are blue smoke on boost or after idling, oil in the intercooler-less charge piping and throttle body, and radial or axial shaft play. A rebuild or replacement installed runs roughly $1,200–2,500, and correct original-style units are increasingly scarce.', 'Timing belt and silent-shaft (balance shaft) belt on the G54B 2.6L (4G54): both belts are rubber, and a failed balance-shaft belt can be thrown into the timing belt and take it out. Original or undocumented belts on a car this age are a must-replace regardless of mileage (roughly 60k miles or 5–7 years). Ask for a receipt listing both belts, tensioners and ideally the water pump and cam/crank seals. Expect $700–1,400 as a package.', "MCA-Jet valves and hydraulic lash adjusters: the head has a third small 'jet' valve per cylinder that needs periodic mechanical clearance adjustment. When neglected it causes rough idle, hard starting and poor emissions. Sticking hydraulic lifters cause a persistent top-end tick. Worn valve stem seals and guides give a puff of blue smoke on cold start or after decel, common at 80k+ miles. A jet-valve adjustment is cheap ($150–300), but top-end work with stem seals or guides runs $1,500–3,000.", 'Head gasket, cylinder head and overheating history: the large 2.6L four in an aging cooling system is vulnerable to head gasket seepage and to cracks between valve seats after overheating. Check for coolant loss, white exhaust, oil/coolant cross-contamination and a combustion-gas (block) test result. A compression or leakdown test is essential. A head job runs $2,000–4,000, more if the head must be sourced.', 'ECI (Electronically Controlled Injection) blow-through throttle body: these non-intercooled cars use a pressurized throttle body with two large injectors fed by the turbo. Injector failure, perished internal gaskets and leaking injector O-rings cause rich running, boost leaks and a genuine fuel-leak fire risk. Injectors and rebuild parts are discontinued or very expensive, often $300–600 per used or refurbished injector. A throttle body rebuild runs roughly $600–1,500. Receipts for a rebuild and new fuel hoses are valuable.', 'Karman-vortex airflow sensor, ECU and sensors: the airflow sensor, idle speed control servo, TPS and the aging ECU (dried capacitors) cause stalling, surging, no-start and erratic idle. Diagnosis on this pre-OBD system is specialist work. A used airflow sensor runs $300–800, and an ECU repair or rebuild about $200–600.', 'Oil leaks and oil cooler lines: the front case, oil pump, cam seal, valve cover/half-moon seals, oil pan and the rubber/steel oil cooler and turbo feed/return lines all seep with age. Hardened cooler lines can burst and dump oil quickly. Line replacement runs about $300–700. Fixing front case or oil pump leaks is labor-intensive, around $600–1,200.', 'Cooling system: aging radiators (often original plastic-tank units), the thermostat housing, heater hoses, water pump and the coolant lines to the retrofit water-cooled turbo all fail. A full refresh with radiator, hoses, thermostat and cap runs $600–1,200 and is cheap insurance against head damage.', 'Fuel tank, sender and pump: an inaccurate or dead fuel gauge is very common and usually means a failed in-tank sender. Rust or varnish inside the tank clogs the pump and filter. A sender/pump service runs $250–700. A replacement tank, if available, can be much more, and decades-old fuel and vapor hoses should be replaced.', "Rust: even on dry-climate cars, check the lower front fenders behind the wheels, rocker panels and rocker covers, rear wheel arches and quarter panels, the spare tire well and

profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Fuel tank sender, pump and tank cleaning if the gauge reads incorrectly or fuel is varnished', 'Valve cover, half-moon, cam seal, oil pan and front case reseals for persistent oil leaks', 'Suspension refresh: strut inserts, control arm and subframe bushings, steering coupler, alignment', 'Clutch hydraulics (master/slave) and possibly the clutch if slipping or the pedal engagement is high', 'A/C system service or R12-to-R134a conversion, compressor seals', 'Pop-up headlight motor/linkage service, ground cleaning, gauge cluster repair', 'Brake caliper rebuilds and parking brake mechanism freeing', 'Turbo inspection and potential rebuild if shaft play or oil seepage is present; wastegate actuator check', 'Exhaust manifold stud replacement or manifold repair if cracked or ticking']
profiles.market_notes: Narrowbody non-intercooled cars are the most affordable Starions. Rough drivers trade around $4–8k, and clean, documented, low-mile manuals bring roughly $10–18k at auction, while widebody ESI-R cars command a clear premium. Original paint and a complete, unmodified drivetrain matter most, while full repaints, aftermarket exhausts, boost or EFI conversions all discount value. The 5-speed manual is strongly preferred over the automatic. Documentation of turbo history, belts, and an intact ECI system adds real value, and LS/LE trim plus factory options such as A/C and an LSD also lift price.
profiles.catchup_notes: Even low-mile examples are 40 years old, so assume all rubber is suspect: fuel, oil-cooler and coolant hoses, belts, bushings, seals, brake hoses and tires. Expect a $2,500–5,000 catch-up pass on a nice car with incomplete records, before any turbo, ECI or rust surprises. Budget extra time and money for scarce ECI and body parts.

profiles.label: Panoz Roadster (early stainless-chassis, Ford 5.0 EFI, 1992–1995, pre-AIV)
profiles.framing: This is a hand-built, low-volume American roadster with roughly 44 built. It pairs a Ford 5.0 HO EFI V8 and a Ford-family manual gearbox with a stainless-steel tube chassis and superformed aluminum body panels. For a Carmel driver it is a raw, Cobra-like weekend car for Highway 1 and Carmel Valley Road. The drivetrain is cheap and well understood. The bespoke body, glass, trim and chassis parts are essentially unobtainable. What matters most is solid chassis and body condition, a car that has been properly recommissioned after sitting, and proof that it can be registered and smog-checked in California. Engine rebuilds matter less, because the Ford hardware is the easy part.
profiles.weak_points: ['Storage and recommissioning risk dominates. Most surviving cars show very low miles, which means decades of sitting. Expect varnished injectors, a weak or failed in-tank fuel pump, a stale or corroded fuel sender and tank interior, and hardened 1990s fuel hoses that degrade with ethanol fuel. Symptoms are hard hot starts, lean surge, fuel smell and a fuel gauge that reads wrong. A proper fuel system refresh runs roughly $800–$2,500, more if the custom tank must be removed or repaired. Ask for dated receipts for the pump, filter, injector cleaning or replacement, and hoses.', 'Ford 5.0 HO EEC-IV drivability problems are common after storage: sticking IAC valve, TPS drift, a dirty or failing MAF if mass-air equipped, vacuum leaks from cracked hoses and the upper/lower intake gaskets, and EGR faults. Symptoms are hunting idle, stalling on decel and a check-engine light. The parts are cheap ($50–$400 each), but diagnosis on a hand-wired car takes time. Ask for KOEO/KOER self-test code results.', 'Age-related engine oil leaks occur even on low-mile cars because seals dry out: rear main seal, timing cover, oil pan gasket, valve covers and intake gaskets. Labor can be higher than on a Mustang because of tight packaging in the small chassis. Budget $500–$3,000 depending on whether the engine or transmission must come out. Check for fresh drips and wet bellhousing seams.', 'Cooling margin is limited. A full-size V8 sits in a short-nose roadster with bespoke radiator and electric fan packaging. Typical failures are an aged radiator core, a weak electric fan or fan relay, a 5.0 water pump weeping at the weep hole, cracked hoses and a sticking thermostat. These cars can creep hot in traffic. A full cooling refresh runs $800–$2,200. Ask for a coolant change date and evidence of a fan and thermostat test.', 'The clutch and gearbox are Ford-family 5-speed parts. Listings cite a Borg-Warner T5, and some claim T45, so confirm the actual box by tag. Known T5 issues are worn 2nd/3rd synchros, a noisy input bearing and the cluster gear. Age-related issues are a dried clutch hydraulic or cable system, a worn throwout bearing and a glazed clutch from sitting. A clutch job runs $1,500–$3,000. A gearbox rebuild or replacement runs $1,500–$3,500, and parts are readily available.', 'The rear axle is a Ford-sourced limited-slip (Traction-Lok-type clutch packs). Sitting and old gear oil cause clutch-pack chatter in tight turns, pinion seal leaks and worn U-joints or driveshaft balance problems. Fluid with friction modifier runs about $150. A clutch-pack rebuild runs $600–$1,500. Confirm the axle type and ratio.', 'The stainless-steel tube chassis resists rust, but inspect welds and mounting tabs for cracks at the suspension pickups, engine and transmission mounts, and cycle-fender bracket attachments. A hand-built frame on a stiff, short-wheelbase car accumulates fatigue. Repair requires a fabricator skilled in stainless TIG welding, roughly $1,000–$5,000 or more. There is no factory support or jig.', 'The aluminum body panels are superformed and not reproduced. Watch for galvanic corrosion where aluminum meets the steel or stainless chassis and fasteners, and for filiform corrosion bubbling under the paint at edges, seams and around hardware. Look for stress cracks at the clamshell hood hinges and latches and at the cycle-fender mounts, which vibrate. Coastal Carmel air accelerates this. Body and paint repair on aluminum by a specialist can easily run $3,000–$10,000 or more. A damaged panel may be irreplaceable.', 'Bespoke trim, glass and lighting are a sourcing problem. The windscreen frame and glass, taillight bezels, chrome trim, gauges, badges, soft top or tonneau, and interior leather pieces are unique or low-volume. The example listing notes a replaced taillight bezel, which shows these parts break and get substituted. Confirm that every unique piece is present and intact. Missing parts may require fabrication or a donor search costing hundreds

profiles.market_notes: With so few cars built, comps are sparse and price is driven mostly by condition, completeness and story. Values move with documentation of the chassis number and provenance (Panoz letters, original invoice, factory or marketing history), intact bespoke trim and body panels, original paint quality, and proof of recent recommissioning. Ultra-low miles on stored cars draw collector bids, but for a driver, mileage matters less than receipts showing the fuel, brake and cooling systems were redone. These early 5.0 cars generally trade below the later AIV Roadsters with the 4.6 DOHC engine. Missing or replaced unique parts, aluminum panel damage and California smog uncertainty are the biggest discounts.
profiles.catchup_notes: A typical example is a low-mile car that has sat for years. Expect a full recommissioning (tires, brakes, fuel system, cooling, all fluids, belts and hoses) costing roughly $2,500–$6,000 before it is a trustworthy driver. After that, the bigger financial exposure is not the Ford drivetrain but irreplaceable aluminum panels, bespoke trim, and possible chassis or electrical surprises on a hand-built car.

profiles.label: Pontiac Solstice GXP (Kappa, 2007-2009, Roadster & Coupe)
profiles.framing: The Solstice GXP is a cheap, rear-drive, manual-transmission roadster with real turbo torque (2.0L LNF direct-injection Ecotec, 260 hp / 260 lb-ft) and hydraulic steering. It suits Highway 1, Carmel Valley Road and Laureles Grade, but it is cramped, has almost no trunk with the top down, and has no spare. Its mechanicals are mostly shared GM parts and are inexpensive. Body panels, top components and Kappa-specific trim are getting scarce, so buy the cleanest unmodified, documented car you can. For a California owner, smog legality of any tune is a first-order issue, not a footnote.
profiles.weak_points: ['Intake valve carbon buildup (LNF direct injection): from roughly 40-60k miles, carbon on the intake valves causes rough cold idle, misfires (P0300-P0304) and lost power. Tuned cars and short-trip cars are worse. The fix is walnut blasting at about $400-800. Look for a record of intake cleaning, or budget for it. A borescope through the intake ports settles the question.', 'Timing chain stretch and tensioner/guide wear: Ecotec chains stretch, especially with extended oil change intervals or the wrong oil. Symptoms are a rattle on cold start for the first few seconds and cam/crank correlation codes P0008, P0016 or P0017. A chain, guide and tensioner job runs about $1,500-2,500. Ask for oil change records at 5k-mile or shorter intervals using GM-spec (dexos/4718M) synthetic, and get the cam/crank correlation values read with a scan tool.', 'High-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) and its cam follower: wear here causes long cranks, stumbling, low-rail-pressure codes (P0087, P0089, P0191) and lean conditions under boost. It is more common on tuned cars. A pump is about $600-1,500 installed. On a tuned car, ask whether the pump and follower have been inspected or replaced.', 'Turbocharger and boost system: the original turbo can develop shaft play, oil seepage at the oil feed and return lines, or wastegate/actuator faults. Boost leaks from charge-pipe couplers popping off or cracking set P0299 (underboost), and the electronic bypass valve can also fail. A turbo replacement runs about $2,000-3,500 installed. A boost leak test is cheap insurance.', 'Cooling system: water pump weeps, thermostat housing leaks, cracked coolant reservoir/degas bottle and Dex-Cool sludge are all common on the Ecotec. Watch for slow coolant loss, a sweet smell, and crust at the pump weep hole or housing. Expect about $500-1,100 for a water pump and thermostat. Look for coolant service records; the 5-year/150k Dex-Cool interval is long past on every car.', 'Clutch and hydraulics (Aisin AR5 5-speed): the concentric slave cylinder can leak, and the clutch slips earlier on tuned or launched cars. The concentric slave sits inside the bellhousing, so replace it whenever the clutch is out. A clutch, slave and flywheel job runs about $1,500-2,400. Look for a clutch receipt, check the engagement point, and do a 3rd/4th-gear pull test for slip. Also check for 2nd/3rd synchro grind on fast shifts.', 'Rear differential: whine, clunk on take-up, pinion and axle seal seepage, and worn diff mount bushings. These are amplified on tuned cars and cars with hard launches. Most cars never have their gear oil changed. A rebuild or used unit runs about $1,200-2,500.', 'Soft top, drains and water intrusion: the top can tear or wear through at fold points, and top latches, tonneau and decklid hardware can break. Clogged rear drains and aging seals let water into the footwells and trunk, which leads to musty carpets, corroded wiring and corrosion around the trunk-mounted battery. A replacement top is about $800-2,000 installed. Ask for photos under the trunk floor and lifted carpet, plus a water test.', "Decklid and hood struts and hinges: the large clamshell decklid and hood struts go weak. They are a cheap fix at about $100-250, but a decklid that won't stay up can damage the top and tonneau mechanism.", "Hydraulic power steering and front suspension: watch for power steering pump whine, rack or hose seepage, front lower control arm bushing wear, sway bar end links and tie rod ends. Clunks over Carmel's broken pavement are typical. Expect about $300-1,200 depending on parts.", 'Window regulators and window indexing: the windows auto-drop slightly to seal against the top. Failed regulators, or lost indexing after a battery disconnect, cause wind noise, leaks and stuck glass. A regulator is about $250-500 per side.', 'Ignition switch recall and other GM campaigns: the 2006-2010 Solstice was included in the GM ignition switch recall campaign. A heavy keyring can turn the key off while driv

profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Intake valve walnut blasting if not documented in the last ~40k miles', 'Coolant drain and refill with Dex-Cool; water pump and thermostat housing if weeping', 'Clutch and concentric slave cylinder if engagement is high or slip appears', 'Front suspension refresh: lower control arm bushings, end links, tie rod ends, then an alignment', 'PCV system inspection and refresh; check for oil in the charge pipes and intercooler', 'Soft top treatment, or replacement if it is torn or wearing through at the folds', 'Window regulator or indexing repair if leaks or wind noise persist', 'Power steering hose or pump reseal if seepage worsens']
profiles.market_notes: The 2009 GXP Coupe (targa) is the rare top tier and commands a strong premium over the roadster. Manual roadsters trade well above the 5L40-E automatic. Mileage bands matter sharply: under ~30k is a collector-adjacent price, 40-80k is the driver sweet spot, and over 100k sells at a steep discount. Unmodified cars with service records outsell tuned cars. A documented dealer-installed GMPP upgrade is neutral to slightly positive, but an unknown tune, aftermarket downpipe or aftermarket head unit is a negative, especially in California. Bright factory colors (Mean Yellow, Aggressive Red) and clean, original interiors without seat covers draw more bidders. Cars with leak or water history, torn tops or salvage titles sell at a deep discount and are hard to resell.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most GXPs are 15+ years old with low annual mileage. Expect deferred age items regardless of the odometer: original or long-overdue coolant, brake fluid, diff and gearbox oil; aging tires and battery; dried-out top seals and clogged drains. Many have never had intake valve cleaning. Budget roughly $1,500-3,000 in catch-up work on a typical 40-70k-mile example even before any wear parts.

profiles.label: Porsche 911 (964) Carrera 2 / Carrera 4
profiles.framing: The 964 is the last usable-everyday air-cooled 911 with modern comforts (power steering, ABS, coil springs, real HVAC) and the raw M64 3.6 character that later cars smooth out. For a Carmel-based driver, this is a weekend Highway 1 and Laureles Grade car that can be driven hard without the anxiety of a six-figure 993 Turbo or a museum-grade 2.7 RS — but only if the engine's known sealing and top-end issues are documented as already addressed. The Carrera 4's extra driveline (front diff, transfer shaft, ABD/ABS hydraulics) adds capability and complexity; a well-sorted C4 is a superb all-weather coastal car, a neglected one is a money pit. Documented, unmodified, with a legible chain of invoices matters far more here than mileage or cosmetics.
profiles.weak_points: Engine case/cylinder oil leaks: the M64's biggest single issue is leaking head studs and, more famously, the dual-row-to-single-row era case and the notorious oil return tube and cylinder-to-case seepage. Most honest 964s weep from the through-bolt/head-stud area and the chain housing gaskets; a proper fix is engine-out, roughly $12,000–$25,000+ depending on whether cylinders/pistons and heads are touched. Look for an engine-out invoice naming head studs (ARP or Raceware), Carrillo/ARP rod bolts, and resealing of the chain housings and cam towers. Dual-mass flywheel: early cars (1989–1991) used a Freudenberg DMF that fails and clatters at idle; later LuK units are better. Failure symptoms are rattle at idle that disappears on clutch engagement; replacement is a transmission-out job, $2,500–$4,500 with clutch. Distributor vent belt (the internal belt linking the twin distributor rotors): if it snaps, the secondary rotor runs unsynchronized, torching the cap and potentially the engine. Later factory vented caps mitigate; there must be a receipt in the last 4–6 years / 30–40k miles or plan $600–$1,200 to inspect and renew. Valve guides and top-end wear: high-mileage M64s (over 100k) smoke on startup and burn oil; a leakdown/compression test is not optional. Head gaskets and studs pulling on high-heat, hard-driven cars are a five-figure repair. Oil cooler and lines: the front-fender-mounted oil cooler and long steel/rubber oil lines corrode and weep; a leaking cooler dumps oil quickly and costs $700–$1,800 plus lines. Air conditioning: original R12 systems converted poorly to R134a are the norm; condensers, evaporator, and hoses all age out and full restoration with a modern condenser/parallel-flow setup runs $2,000–$4,000. Carrera 4 specific: the front differential and transfer/center driveshaft leak and the ABD/PDAS hydraulic unit and its accumulator fail — a failed C4 hydraulic pump or pressure accumulator triggers ABS/brake warning lights and parts are scarce and expensive ($1,500–$4,000). C4 front CV/axle boots and the front driveshaft support are common leak points. Motor/transmission mounts sag (many owners fit 993-spec mounts, as this car has), causing shifter vibration. Suspension bushings, control-arm ball joints, and rear spring plate bushings are all 30 years old on original cars; a full refresh with Bilsteins runs $3,000–$6,000. Airbag/pedal box: the 964 pedal cluster bushings wear and the clutch pedal bracket cracks — a known and cheap-to-fix but commonly ignored item. Electrics: the alarm/central locking control unit, power window regulators, HVAC control head (blend flap servos and the vacuum-operated system) and instrument cluster board solder joints all fail; the odometer gears crack and the speedo needs a rebuild ($400–$800). Rust: 964s are galvanized and generally sound, but check the front trunk floor/battery tray, the sunroof drains and the A-pillar corners, the base of the windshield (leaks from resealed or replaced windshields cause rot under the dash), and the rear torsion tube area. Fuel system: rubber fuel hoses and the fuel-line rail under the tank harden; fire risk on cars without replacement records. Finally, at 150k+ miles the five-speed G64 transaxle's second-gear synchro wears — notchy 2nd on a cold car is normal, a crunch under load is not; a rebuild is $5,000–$8,000.
profiles.immediate_repairs: Full fluid service (Mobil 1 15W-50 or equivalent, ~11 quarts, filter, drain plug seals), valve adjustment if not documented within 15k miles, new fuel filter, inspect and likely replace the distributor vent belt and both caps/rotors if the receipt is older than five years, replace hardened fuel and vacuum hoses, four-wheel alignment after any suspension work, check and correct tire age (anything over six years replaced regardless of tread), A/C evacuate/recharge and leak test, and a full diagnostic scan of the DME and — on a C4 — the ABS/ABD hydraulic system. Expect to chase at least one small oil leak (chain housing, oil return tubes, or a cooler line) and to service or rebuild the pedal box bushings.
profiles.repairs_12mo: Clutch and dual-mass flywheel if not recently replaced, motor and transmission mounts if still original, front and rear shock/strut refresh and rubber bushings if undocumented, oil cooler and hard lines if any seepage, A/C condenser and hoses for reliable coastal-summer function, power window regulators and central locking control unit, HVAC blend/flap servos, brake flex lines and full fluid flush (and ABS accumulator on the C4 if pressure warning appears), and on higher-mileage cars a transaxle reseal and possible 2nd-gear synchro attention. Budget for a set of correct-size Michelin or Pirelli N-rated tires and a proper corner-balance/alignment.
profiles.market_notes: Coupes with a manual outsell Tiptronics by a wide margin and Tiptronic C2s trade at a steep discount; Carrera 4 coupes historically sat below C2s but factory widebody (Turbo-look, option M491) cars are genuinely rare and command a large premium, as do RS Americas, Turbos, and Speedsters. Documented engine-out top-end work with head studs is worth real money and its absence should be priced in at $15,000–$25,000 regardless of how the car presents. Original paint and matching numbers matter, but a well-executed, fully invoiced refurbishment with photos from a known shop is acceptable to a driver-buyer; unverifiable 'restored' claims, respray over filler, and mileage discrepancies (or a Carfax that misidentifies the model, as in the example listing) are where money is lost. High-mileage cars are acceptable at the right price if the service chain is continuous; six-figure asks on a 170k-mile C4 rest entirely on the quality and verifiability of the rebuild paperwork.
profiles.catchup_notes: A typical 30-plus-year-old 964 needs everything rubber renewed: fuel and vacuum hoses, brake flex lines, engine and transmission mounts, suspension bushings, window and door seals, and the A/C system. Even a freshly refurbished example will need a shakedown cycle of fluid services, a valve adjustment, alignment, and chasing small leaks over the first few thousand miles, plus tires if the date codes are past six years.

profiles.label: Porsche 911 Carrera (991.2, 2017-2019)
profiles.framing: For a Carmel buyer, the 991.2 Carrera is a usable, comfortable, modern 911 for Highway 1, Carmel Valley Road and longer Central Coast runs. Its 9A2 3.0L twin-turbo flat-six avoids the IMS and bore-scoring worries tied to earlier water-cooled cars. The real risks are drivetrain abuse (over-revs, clutch wear on manuals), the turbo and charge-air system, and expensive optional chassis hardware (front-axle lift, rear-axle steering, PASM). Low-mileage examples often skip age-based maintenance, so dated records and a recent full PIWIS scan matter more than the odometer.
profiles.weak_points: ['Over-rev history: the DME logs over-rev events in ranges 1-6. On 7-speed manual cars, a money-shift (e.g., 5th to 2nd instead of 4th) shows up as range 3+ events and can damage valvetrain or bearings with no outward sign. Range 1-2 hits are usually rev-limiter bounces and benign. Several range 4+ events, or any range 5-6 event, is a serious concern. Get a recent printout that includes engine hours and ignition counts, not a years-old screenshot.', 'Turbocharger and wastegate: 9A2 turbos are generally durable. Some cars develop a wastegate rattle, which is a metallic buzz or chatter on cold start or tip-in that fades when warm. It can be just an annoyance or can progress to an actuator or turbo replacement. Out of warranty, a single turbo runs about $5,000-9,000 at a dealer, and both about $10,000-15,000. Look for oil film in the charge pipes, smoke on cold start, and charge-pressure fault codes.', 'Charge-air plumbing: intercooler hoses, couplers and clamps can loosen or crack. Symptoms are a hiss under boost, limp mode, or underboost and charge-pressure codes. The fix is usually $200-1,000. Check for evidence of aftermarket tunes or intake parts, which also complicate California smog compliance without a CARB EO.', 'Front radiators and A/C condensers: the three front-mounted radiators and the condensers trap leaves and road debris behind the bumper openings. That debris holds moisture and corrodes the cores, which matters with coastal Carmel air. Expect roughly $600-1,500 per condenser or radiator installed. Ask for photos of the openings or a record of a nose cleaning, and watch for weak A/C or rising coolant temps.', '7-speed manual clutch and dual-mass flywheel: clutch life depends heavily on driving. Hill starts, valet abuse and launching all shorten it. A clutch with DMF and slave cylinder runs about $4,500-7,000. Check engagement height, slip in 4th-5th under full load, judder on take-off, and DMF rattle at idle. Notchy or vague shifting can come from cable adjustment rather than internal wear.', "PDK (if equipped): the 7-speed PDK is robust. Watch for harsh low-speed engagement, hesitation from a stop, or mechatronic faults, and confirm the fluid has been serviced per Porsche's age/mileage schedule (roughly 6 years). PIWIS can read clutch wear values. Mechatronic or clutch-pack work can reach $4,000-10,000+.", 'PASM dampers: the adaptive dampers (standard on S/GTS, optional on base and T) can weep oil. Symptoms are a clunk over sharp bumps or a bouncy corner. Expect about $1,200-2,000 per corner installed for OEM parts. Inspect each shock body for a wet film.', 'Front-axle lift system (optional): the hydraulic pump and lift struts can fail or leak, and that matters for Carmel driveways and ramps, especially if a front lip has been added. Repair runs about $1,500-3,500. Cycle it several times on the PPI.', 'Rear-axle steering (optional on S/GTS/T): the rear-steer actuators can fault. Look for a warning light, a stuck straight-ahead mode, or a clunk at low speed. Each side costs about $2,500-4,000. Confirm it is active with no stored faults.', 'Direct-injection carbon buildup: the 9A2 is direct-injection only, so the intake valves carbon up with miles and short trips. You may see rough idle or misfire codes past about 50-70k miles. Walnut blasting costs about $1,000-1,800. Cylinder bore scoring is rare on the 9A2, but a borescope is cheap insurance on high-mileage or tracked cars.', 'Oil and coolant leaks: watch for seepage at the rear main seal, the valve-cover/cam-housing area, turbo oil feed and return lines, and the coolant hoses, water pump and expansion tank as cars pass 50-80k miles or 8+ years. Most are $500-2,500 jobs. Some 9A2 engines use measurable oil between services, so ask about top-ups.', 'Ignition and age-based maintenance: spark plugs (roughly 4 years/30-40k miles, about $700-1,100), coil packs, accessory drive belt, brake fluid every 2 years, and an annual oil service are often missed on low-mileage

Staggered 20-inch N-rated tires run about $1,800-2,600 mounted.', '12V AGM battery test and replacement with coding if weak or original (about $400-650). Low-mileage cars often sit.', 'Engine and cabin air filters if undocumented (about $150-350).', 'Front radiator and condenser debris cleanout through the bumper openings, with core inspection (about $300-700).', 'Clear or diagnose any stored f
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Spark plugs, and coils as needed, if near the roughly 4-year/30-40k interval with no record (about $700-1,500).', 'Accessory drive belt per the age/mileage schedule (about $200-400).', 'Replacement of any weeping PASM damper (about $1,200-2,000 per corner).', 'A/C condenser or radiator replacement if corrosion is found on inspection (about $600-1,500 each).', 'Rear decklid struts if weak (about $150-300).', 'PDK fluid service if equipped and approaching about 6 years with no record (about $800-1,200).', 'Coolant hose, water pump or expansion tank seepage repair if noted on the PPI (about $500-1,800).', 'Front-end stone-chip repair or PPF refresh for coastal and highway driving (about $500-2,500).']
profiles.market_notes: The 7-speed manual carries a clear premium over PDK across trims, with the lightweight-focused Carrera T and the GTS strongest. A Carrera S typically commands several thousand dollars over a comparable base car. Paint-to-sample and special colors (Miami Blue, Lava Orange, Chalk) and desirable options (Sport Chrono, sport exhaust, PASM, front-axle lift, rear-axle steering) lift value, while modifications, aftermarket brakes or aero, and missing receipts narrow the buyer pool. Mileage bands under 20k, 20-50k and over 50k move price noticeably, and a clean California history, a recent DME report, dated annual service records and Porsche CPO eligibility all support a premium.
profiles.catchup_notes: 991.2 cars are now roughly 7-9+ years old, and low-mileage examples routinely miss time-based items: brake fluid, spark plugs, drive belt, tires and battery. PDK fluid is also often overdue. Budget about $2,500-5,000 to bring a typical low-mile car current, more if tires and plugs are both due.

profiles.label: Porsche 911 Carrera (993, naturally aspirated)
profiles.framing: The 993 is the last air-cooled 911. For this buyer it is a usable, analog weekend and canyon car on Highway 1 and Carmel Valley Road, not a garage queen. The most important questions are the health of the cylinder heads and valve guides, and whether the car will pass a California smog check and register cleanly. That matters for any out-of-state car, and especially for 1996-98 OBD-II cars with the secondary air injection (SAI) problem. Documented, unmodified, rust-free examples with a clear oil-consumption and leakdown story are worth a real premium over cheaper cars with unknown top ends.
profiles.weak_points: ["Valve guide wear is the big-ticket 993 failure. It typically shows at 70k-130k miles, earlier on cars that sat or were driven gently. Symptoms are blue smoke on cold start or after idling at lights, oil use worse than about 1 qt per 1,000 miles, and a fouled plug or two. Leakdown can look acceptable while the guides are worn, so a guide 'wiggle' check needs the engine apart. A top-end rebuild (heads, guides, valves, gaskets) runs $12k-$22k at a good independent and much more with machine-shop surprises. Look for receipts naming the specific work: guides, valve job, head gaskets.", 'Secondary air injection (SAI) on 1996-98 OBD-II cars. Carbon clogs the small air passages in the cylinder heads, setting P0410/P0411 and a check-engine light, which fails a California smog check. In-car port cleaning or drilling costs $1,500-$4,000 and does not always last. The permanent fix is heads-off, usually combined with a top-end job. Ask for proof the SAI monitor has been run and passed, not just codes cleared before the sale.', 'Oil leaks are near-universal on age. Common sources are the lower valve cover gaskets, chain housing covers, the oil return tubes between case and heads, the oil pressure sender and switch, the oil cooler seals, and the rear main seal. Leaks on hot exhaust or heat exchangers create smoke and smell. Valve cover reseals cost $800-$2,000. A rear main seal needs the transmission out ($1,500-$2,500, more if a clutch is done at the same time). Look for recent reseal receipts and photos of a dry underside.', 'Front oil cooler, lines, and fan. The right-front fender oil cooler, its long hard lines to the engine, and the thermostatically controlled cooler fan corrode and fail with age. Watch for corroded or weeping line fittings, oil residue in the right-front wheel well, and a fan that never cycles when hot. Lines cost $1,500-$3,000 installed. A cooler or fan costs $400-$1,200.', 'Manual cars: the dual-mass flywheel (DMF) and clutch. DMF wear shows as rattle at idle that stops when the clutch is pressed, plus chatter on take-off. Clutch and DMF together cost about $3,000-$4,500. Also check the shift linkage bushings and the clutch hydraulics. The 6-speed G50/21 gearbox is otherwise robust; check for second- and third-gear synchro crunch on fast shifts.', 'Tiptronic cars: the 4-speed Tiptronic S is generally durable but ages. Watch for harsh or delayed 1-2 and 2-3 shifts, flare on upshift, slipping, delayed engagement into D or R, and electronic faults that disable Tip mode. Much depends on fluid service history. A rebuild or valve-body repair runs $4,000-$8,000. Tiptronic also cuts resale value sharply, which is a cost if the buyer ever sells.', "Rust is limited on this galvanized body, but it does exist. The classic 993 rust is in the windshield and rear window frame corners under the seals. Repair requires glass removal, metal work, and paint ($3,000-$8,000). Also check the front trunk floor, battery box, door bottoms, and the area near the fuel tank. Carmel's salt air makes later bubbling a real concern. Corner rust visible in photos usually means more under the seal.", 'Ignition and DME. The 993 is twin-plug with twin distributors. Distributor cap, rotor, and drive-belt wear, along with moisture buildup, cause misfires; a vent kit and distributor service cost $500-$1,500. Twelve plugs and wires cost $900-$1,600 because of labor. The DME relay is a classic no-start or stalling cause; carry a $50-$100 spare.', '1996+ alarm, immobilizer, and central locking. Remote fob, alarm module, and immobilizer faults cause no-start and intermittent locking problems. Check that all keys and fobs work and that the immobilizer releases reliably. A replacement fob with programming costs $300-$800. Module repair costs $300-$1,000.', 'Climate control. The automatic heater controller fails (the example car just had it replaced). Other failures include the heater flap cables and actuators, heater blower motor ($600-$1,200), and auxiliary f
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['California smog pre-check or OBD-II readiness scan before or immediately after purchase. Resolve any SAI or catalytic converter codes before registration deadlines.', 'Engine oil and filter with the correct air-cooled spec oil; check oil level hot, on level ground, idling.', 'Transmission fluid: gear oil for manuals, or Tiptronic ATF plus final-drive oil, if not documented in the last 2 years.', 'Brake fluid flush and inspection of pads, rotors, and hoses.', 'Fan belt and alternator belt inspection or replacement, plus the AC belt.', 'Spare DME relay. Inspect the distributor cap, rotor, and vent, and the condition of the plugs and wires.', 'Battery and charging-system check; fit a battery maintainer if the car will sit.', 'Tire age check by DOT date; replace if over 6 years, regardless o
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Valve cover gasket, chain cover, and oil return tube reseal if leaking.', 'Spark plugs and plug wires (12) if not documented in the last 30k miles or 5 years.', 'Distributor service and vent kit if not previously done.', 'Front oil cooler line replacement if the fittings are corroded or weeping.', 'Suspension refresh: shocks, front control arm and rear LSA bushings, strut mounts, engine and transmission mounts.', 'AC service, front condenser fan, and possible condenser or evaporator work.', 'Heater blower and heater flap cable or actuator repairs.', 'Window regulators, sunroof cable and drain service, and rear spoiler motor or cable service.', 'Manual cars: plan for a clutch and DMF if rattle or chatter is present.', 'Corrosion treatment of the windshield and rear window corners if early
profiles.market_notes: Transmission is the biggest single value lever. Manual 6-speed Carrera coupes trade at roughly a 35-50% premium over Tiptronic cars, and Tip coupes sit at the bottom of the coupe market. Wide-body Carrera S and Carrera 4S (and the Targa to some collectors) carry big premiums over a base Carrera 2; Cabriolets trade lower. Paint-to-sample and desirable colors such as Speed Yellow, Riviera Blue, Arena Red, and Guards Red outperform silver and black. Mileage bands below 50k and 50-90k move price, but a documented top end (guides and SAI), a dry engine, no rust, and a clean ownership history matter more for a driver. Many owners, repossession or title anomalies, and visible corner rust should pull the price down materially.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most 993s are 27-30 years old, and even well-kept ones need some age-related catch-up: rubber (seals, bushings, mounts, boots), oil leak reseals, ignition service, climate-control repairs, and fluids. A typical example with incomplete records should be budgeted at $5,000-$10,000 of catch-up work in the first year, on top of the risk reserve for a top end or SAI fix. Out-of-state cars also need to clear California smog before registration, so SAI and catalyst health should be confirmed up front.

profiles.label: Porsche 911 Carrera (996.1, 1999–2001, 3.4L)
profiles.framing: The 996.1 is the cheapest way into a proper water-cooled 911. It has a 296 hp 3.4L M96 flat-six, a cable throttle, and a stout G96 six-speed. For a Carmel buyer it makes a rewarding Highway 1 and Carmel Valley driver. The catch is that it carries the most engine-design risk of any modern 911. The car is judged almost entirely on engine health evidence (IMS status, filter and borescope results, coolant/oil separation) and on proof of sympathetic maintenance. Cosmetics, options, and miles matter much less. Buy the best-documented, unmodified, CA-smog-passable manual car you can, and keep a real reserve for the engine.
profiles.weak_points: ['IMS bearing: 1999 and most early-2000 cars use the dual-row sealed intermediate shaft bearing. Its failure rate is low (roughly 1%) but a failure is catastrophic. Late-2000 and 2001 builds moved to the weaker single-row bearing, with failure rates of several percent. When the bearing fails it sheds debris and lets the timing go, and the usual result is a scrapped or rebuilt engine at $15k–25k+. The fix is an LN Engineering IMS Retrofit or IMS Solution, typically done with the clutch. Expect $1,000–2,000 over the clutch job, or $3,000–4,500 standalone. Documentation: an invoice naming the specific retrofit part and the shop. Production month on the door-jamb sticker tells you which bearing it left the factory with.', "Cracked or slipped cylinder liners and porous blocks/heads (3.4L M96.01 specific): early 3.4 engines are known for liner cracks (the 'D-chunk'), slipped liners, and porous castings that let coolant and oil mix. Symptoms are unexplained coolant loss, a milky film under the oil cap or in the expansion tank, white smoke, and overheating under load. A cure means an engine rebuild or replacement, roughly $12k–25k. Look for a documented factory replacement engine (common on these years, often with updated parts), coolant pressure-test results, and oil analysis showing no glycol.", 'Bore scoring: much rarer on the 3.4 than on the 3.6/3.8 engines, but it does happen. It shows up as one exhaust bank sooting black, a lazy tick that persists when warm, oil consumption, and low compression or high leakdown, usually on cylinders 4–6. Only a borescope confirms it. An engine-out repair (Nikasil sleeves or a new block) runs $15k+. Ask for borescope images of all six cylinders.', 'Rear main seal (RMS) leak: chronic on M96 engines. The classic sign is a drip at the engine/transaxle junction. An updated seal is cheap (about $50 in parts) but needs the transmission out, so it gets bundled with the clutch, DMF, and IMS work. A light weep is acceptable. A pool under the car or oil on the clutch is not. Look for receipts showing the updated-seal part number.', 'Dual-mass flywheel and clutch: original LuK DMFs are now 20+ years old and commonly delaminate. Signs are rattle or chatter at idle that goes away with the clutch pedal pressed, and clunking on/off throttle. A full clutch, DMF, RMS, and IMS job at a Monterey/Bay Area independent runs about $4,500–7,500. A car with known DMF chatter, like the example listing, should be priced as needing this full job.', 'Air-oil separator (AOS): failure causes a big cloud of smoke at startup or after cornering, high crankcase vacuum (the oil filler cap is hard to pull), a rough idle, and a CEL. It can hydrolock the engine in extreme cases. Expect $400–900. Ask whether and when it was replaced.', 'Cooling system: the water pump bearing seeps and early impellers degrade, so pumps are replaced proactively every 60k miles or 6–8 years. The thermostat is done at the same time, for $700–1,400 total. The coolant expansion tank cracks along its seams and drips onto the engine, about $250–500. The front-mounted radiators and AC condensers trap leaves and corrode, about $1,200–2,800 for the set, along with fan and fan-resistor failures. Cooling neglect directly accelerates the engine failures above. Look for receipts covering the water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, and radiators.', 'Variocam, timing chains, and cam timing: chain tensioner pads and guides wear, and Variocam solenoids or adjusters fail (P1xxx codes, rough idle). Have a PIWIS or Durametric scan check the cam deviation values; sloppy values point to chain or guide wear. Note that ME5.2-era 996.1 DMEs generally cannot give a usable over-rev report like 2002+ cars, so mechanical evidence matters more.', 'Oil leaks beyond the RMS: cam cover gaskets, spark plug tube seals, and the oil pump seal all leak. Expect $800–2,000 depending on scope. Oil fouling of the spark plug tubes causes misfires.', 'Ignition: coil packs crack from heat (misfire
profiles.immediate_repairs: ['Full fluid baseline: engine oil (5W-40 A40-rated, 5k-mile or annual interval going forward) with the filter cut open and inspected, plus oil analysis. Also brake fluid flush, transaxle fluid, and coolant if records are vague. About $500–1,000.', "IMS decision: if there's no retrofit receipt, plan the LN retrofit or Solution. Do it with the clutch if the clutch or DMF is near end of life. About $3,000–4,500 standalone, or $4,500–7,500 bundled with clutch, DMF, and RMS.", 'Serpentine belt, idler and tensioner pulleys, and the air filter if age is unknown. About $250–500.', 'Spark plugs and inspection of the coil packs for cracks. Replace if original or unknown. About $500–1,100.', 'Remove the front bumper cover to clean the radiators and condensers and check for corrosion. About $200–400 f
profiles.repairs_12mo: ['Water pump and thermostat if no record within ~60k miles or 6–8 years. About $700–1,400.', 'Front radiators and AC condensers if corroded or leaking. About $1,200–2,800.', 'Air-oil separator if original or showing symptoms. About $400–900.', 'Front control arms, rear toe links, and engine/transmission mounts. About $1,000–2,500.', 'Cam cover or spark plug tube seal leaks and any minor oil leaks. About $800–2,000.', 'HVAC blower or final-stage resistor, window regulators, and door lock actuators as they fail. About $200–900 each.', 'Shocks and struts if original. About $1,500–3,000.', 'Cabriolet: top hydraulics or rear window service. About $800–4,000.']
profiles.market_notes: Manual coupes command the most; Tiptronic cars and Cabriolets trade at a clear discount. The Carrera 4 is roughly at par with the C2, and the Millennium Edition C4 (Violet Chromaflair) carries a premium. Documented IMS retrofit work, a factory replacement engine, or a fresh clutch/DMF/RMS job is worth several thousand dollars, as are a thick service file and an unmodified, CA-smog-ready configuration. Driver-quality manual coupes in the 60k–120k-mile band typically sit around $20k–32k. Exceptional low-mile examples in desirable colors (Speed Yellow, Zenith Blue, Arena Red, Ocean Blue) bring $35k–45k+. Arctic Silver and black are common and don't carry premiums. Sport seats, an LSD, the M030 suspension, and the factory aero kit add modestly.
profiles.catchup_notes: Most 996.1s are now 23–26 years old and have stretched oil intervals, original cooling parts, and aged rubber in their history. Expect a typical example to need IMS, clutch/DMF/RMS, cooling system, AOS, and suspension catch-up totaling roughly $6,000–12,000 unless receipts prove recent completion. Budget accordingly even on a clean-looking car.
